children.translated_text: <s>Rasamañjarī</s>, Chapter 1.
May that <s>Gaṇapati</s> grant you auspiciousness — from whose cheek-sphere a drop of honey-liquid flows, upon which a delicate, graceful row of bees, intoxicated from drinking, [rests],

children.text: yadguñjitena vinihanti navendranīla śaṅkāṃ sa vo gaṇapatiḥ śivamātanotu // Rmañj_1.1 //
children.translated_text: and by whose humming he dispels the doubt that [the bees are] fresh sapphires. (1.1)
She who becomes an <s>indīvara</s> (blue lotus) at the lotus-pair of the feet of the foremost deity of <s>Purandara</s>'s (<s>Indra</s>'s) city,

children.text: vandārutā kalayatāṃ sukirīṭakoṭiḥ śrī śāradā bhavatu sā bhavapāradāya // Rmañj_1.2 //
children.translated_text: may that <s>Śrī Śāradā</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>), whose beautiful crown-crests are served by those who worship [her], be [the means] for crossing the ocean of existence. (1.2)

children.text: he bhasmāṅgaviraktirūpaguṇadaṃ taṃ preraṇādaṃ śivaṃ gaṅgābhūṣitaśekharaṃ smaraharaṃ śaktisvarūpaṃ prabho /
children.translated_text: O <s>Śiva</s>, whose form of detachment is marked with sacred ash, who bestows virtuous qualities, that impeller, whose crest is adorned with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, destroyer of <s>Smara</s> (Love), whose essential nature is <s>Śakti</s>, O Lord,

children.text: tvāmīśaṃ karuṇārṇavaṃ śaraṇadaṃ vidyānidhiṃ nirguṇaṃ sūtendraṃ girijāpatiṃ śaśidharaṃ māṅgalyadevaṃ namaḥ /
children.translated_text: to you, <s>Īśa</s>, ocean of compassion, granter of refuge, treasury of knowledge, beyond qualities, lord of <s>sūtas</s> (mercury), lord of <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), bearer of the crescent moon, auspicious deity — salutation!

children.text: śrīvaidyanāthatanayaḥ sunayaḥ suśīlaḥ śrīśālinātha iti viśrutanāmadheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Śālinātha</s>, son of <s>Śrī Vaidyanātha</s>, of good conduct and good character, of widely renowned name,

children.text: tenāvalokya vidhivad vividhaprabandhān ārambhate sukṛtinā rasamañjarīyam // Rmañj_1.3 //
children.translated_text: having duly examined various treatises, this meritorious one commences the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>. (1.3)
The constant practice of good honey-bees of assemblies, always captivating the mind,
this <s>Rasamañjarī</s> (Cluster of Essences), filled with manifold <s>rasas</s> (essences/mercury preparations), is being composed. (1.4)

children.text: harati sakalarogānmūrchito yo narāṇāṃ vitarati kila baddhaḥ khecaratvaṃ javena /
children.translated_text: <s>Pārada</s> (mercury) — which, when swooned [i.e., killed/calcined], destroys all diseases of humans, and which, when bound [i.e., fixed], swiftly bestows the power of moving through the sky,

children.text: sakalasuramunīndrair vanditaṃ śambhubījaṃ sa jayati bhavasindhuḥ pāradaḥ pārado'yam // Rmañj_1.5 //
children.translated_text: venerated by all gods and great sages, the seed of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — that <s>pārada</s> (mercury), the ocean of existence's ferryman, triumphs! (1.5)
Just as fire burns a great heap of dry fuel,
so does this <s>sūta</s> (mercury) burn diseases arising from the three <s>doṣas</s>. (1.6)

children.text: tejo mṛgāṅkamaule soḍhuṃ yannaiva tejasāṃ puñjaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That radiance of the moon-crested one (<s>Śiva</s>) which even clusters of radiances cannot endure,

children.text: ajarāmaratāṃ vitarati kalpataruṃ ca raseśvaraṃ vande // Rmañj_1.7 //
children.translated_text: which bestows freedom from old age and death — I venerate <s>Raseśvara</s> (the Lord of Mercury), the wish-fulfilling tree. (1.7)
He who does not know <s>rasa</s> (mercury), the ocean of compassion, the essence of <s>Hariharātmaka</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Śiva</s> combined),

children.text: vṛthā cikitsāṃ kurute sa vaidyo hāsyatāṃ vrajet // Rmañj_1.8 //
children.translated_text: that physician who performs treatment in vain shall become a laughingstock. (1.8)
He who performs [alchemical] work without service to a guru, being of deluded mind,

children.text: sa yāti niṣphalatvaṃ hi svapnalabdhadhanaṃ yathā // Rmañj_1.9 //
children.translated_text: attains fruitlessness indeed, like wealth obtained in a dream. (1.9)
Those who wish to seize knowledge through theft, deception, force, and the like —
for them, nothing succeeds — neither gems, mantras, nor medicines. (1.10)
One accomplished in mantras, of great valor, steadfast, devoted to <s>Śiva</s>,
devoted to the Goddess, always courageous, intent upon the worship of deities — (1.11)
one who knows the true essence of all sciences, skilled in the work of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) —
one possessing these characteristics should be a guru of <s>rasavidyā</s> (the science of mercury). (1.12)
The disciple should be devoted to his own guru, truthful in speech, firm in his vows,
free from laziness, knowledgeable in his own <s>dharma</s>, and intent upon the worship of the Goddess. (1.13)
Names of <s>pārada</s> (mercury):
<s>Śivabīja</s> (seed of <s>Śiva</s>), <s>sūtarāja</s> (king of mercury), <s>pārada</s>, and <s>rasendraka</s> —

children.text: etāni rasanāmāni tathānyāni śive yathā // Rmañj_1.14 //
children.translated_text: these are the names of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), and there are others as [found] in the <s>Śiva</s> [tantra]. (1.14)
That which is internally deep-blue and externally brilliant, with a radiance resembling the midday sun,

children.text: śasto'tha dhūmraḥ paripāṇḍuraśca citro na yojyo rasakarmasiddhaye // Rmañj_1.15 //
children.translated_text: is commended; but that which is smoky or very pale or variegated should not be used for the accomplishment of mercurial operations. (1.15)
When <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is freed from defects, then it removes death and disease;

children.text: sākṣādamṛtam evaiṣa doṣayukto raso viṣam // Rmañj_1.16 //
children.translated_text: it is verily <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) itself; but mercury with defects is poison. (1.16)
Defects of <s>pārada</s> (mercury):
<s>Nāga</s> (lead), <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), <s>agnicāpalya</s> (instability in fire), <s>asahyatva</s> (intractability), <s>viṣa</s> (poison), <s>giri</s> (ite),

children.text: malā hyete ca vijñeyā doṣāḥ pāradasaṃsthitāḥ // Rmañj_1.17 //
children.translated_text: and <s>mala</s> (impurity) — these should be known as the defects residing in <s>pārada</s> (mercury). (1.17)

children.text: jāḍyaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ mahādāhaṃ vīryanāśaṃ ca mūrcchanām /
children.translated_text: They cause in humans, in sequence: stupor, leprosy, great burning, loss of potency, fainting,

children.text: mṛtyuṃ sphoṭaṃ rogapuñjaṃ kurvantyete kramānnṛṇām // Rmañj_1.18 //
children.translated_text: death, eruptions, and a host of diseases. (1.18)
Purification of <s>pārada</s> (mercury):
Now I shall describe the purification of <s>pārada</s> (mercury);

children.text: raso grāhyaḥ sunakṣatre palānāṃ śatamātrakam // Rmañj_1.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>rasa</s> (mercury) should be taken under an auspicious constellation, in the quantity of a hundred <s>palas</s>. (1.19)
Or fifty, or twenty-five, or ten, or five, or even one —

children.text: palād ūnaṃ na kartavyaṃ rasasaṃskāramuttamam // Rmañj_1.20 //
children.translated_text: but less than one <s>pala</s>, the excellent refinement of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) should not be performed. (1.20)
Purification of <s>pārada</s> (method 1):
Three <s>palas</s> of <s>citraka</s> (leadwort) and mustard seeds, [ground] with the decoctions of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), <s>kanyā</s> (aloe vera), and <s>bṛhatī</s> (nightshade),
the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) triturated for three days is freed from the five impurities and other defects. (1.21)
Purification of <s>pārada</s> (method 2):
With powders of brick-dust and <s>rajanī</s> (turmeric), [in the proportion of] one-sixteenth of the <s>rasa</s> (mercury),
one should triturate it in a mortar for a day with the juice of lemon. (1.22)
General purification of defects:
Washing <s>sūta</s> (mercury) with <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) removes the defect of <s>nāga</s> (lead);
with powder of <s>viśālā</s> and <s>aṅkola</s>, it removes the defect of <s>vaṅga</s> (tin). (1.23)

children.text: rājavṛkṣo malaṃ hanti pāvako hanti pāvakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājavṛkṣa</s> (cassia) destroys <s>mala</s> (impurity); fire destroys [the defect of] fire [instability];
<s>kṛṣṇadhattūra</s> (black thorn-apple) [removes] fickleness; <s>triphalā</s> (the three fruits) destroys poison. (1.24)
The three pungents (<s>kaṭutraya</s>) destroy <s>giri</s> (ite); <s>trikaṇṭaka</s> (tribulus) [destroys] intractability;

children.text: pratidoṣaṃ palāṃśena tatra sūtaṃ sakāñjikam // Rmañj_1.25 //
children.translated_text: for each defect, [use] the [respective remedy] in the proportion of one <s>pala</s>, with <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel). (1.25)
Freed from all defects, divested of the seven sheaths,
this pure <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is produced — employ it in all [alchemical] operations. (1.26)
Purification of <s>pārada</s> (method 2):
Having filtered <s>sūta</s> (mercury) through fine cloth, cast it into a mortar and triturate;

children.text: uddhṛtya cāranālena mṛdbhāṇḍe kṣālayet sudhīḥ // Rmañj_1.27 //
children.translated_text: then the wise one should extract it with <s>aranāla</s> (sour rice-water) and wash it in an earthen vessel. (1.27)

children.text: rasasya daśamāṃśaṃ tu gandhaṃ dattvā vimardayet /
children.translated_text: Adding <s>gandha</s> (sulphur) in the measure of one-tenth of the <s>rasa</s> (mercury), one should triturate
with lemon juice for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours); it should be distilled in a distillation apparatus. (1.28)

children.text: punar mardyaṃ punaḥ pātyaṃ saptavāraṃ viśuddhaye /
children.translated_text: It should be triturated again and distilled again, seven times for purification;

children.text: yuktaṃ sarvasya sūtasya taptakhalve vimardanam // Rmañj_1.29 //
children.translated_text: it is proper to triturate all <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in a heated mortar. (1.29)
The heated mortar (<s>taptakhalva</s>):
One should place goat-dung, husk, and fire underground in a pit, [arranging] the three [in layers];
the mortar placed on top of that is known as the heated mortar (<s>taptakhalva</s>). (1.30)
Purification of <s>pārada</s>:
One should triturate <s>sūta</s> (mercury) for a day with <s>kumārī</s> (aloe) and <s>niśā</s> (turmeric) powders;
distilling it in a distillation apparatus, the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes properly purified. (1.31)
Purification of <s>pārada</s>:
<s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s> (sandalwood) and <s>devadāru</s> (deodar cedar), <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> (a plant), and the juices of <s>jayā</s>,
<s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>musalī</s>, and <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) — adding the juice, one should triturate. (1.32)
One should triturate for one day, and then employ the purified [mercury].
Purification of <s>pārada</s>:

children.text: athavā hiṅgulāt sūtaṃ grāhayet tannigadyate // Rmañj_1.33 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, mercury should be extracted from <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) — that is now described. (1.33)
<s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) triturated for a day with the juice of lemon and neem,
by means of an upward-distillation apparatus — pure <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is obtained. (1.34)
Freed from the sheaths of <s>nāga</s> (lead), <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), and others in mercurial operations,
even without the eightfold procedures, this <s>sūta</s> (mercury) accomplishes all operations. (1.35)

children.text: sarvasiddhamatam etad īritaṃ sūtaśuddhikaram adbhutaṃ param /
children.translated_text: This, accepted by all <s>siddhas</s> (adepts), has been declared — marvelously supreme for the purification of <s>sūta</s> (mercury);
bestowing great accomplishments through simple procedures, it is praised for the transformation of the body and metals. (1.36)

children.text: saṃskārahīnaṃ khalu sūtarājaṃ yaḥ sevate tasya karoti bādhām /
children.translated_text: He who uses the king of <s>sūtas</s> (mercury) without [proper] refinement — it causes harm to him;

children.text: dehasya nāśaṃ vividhaṃ ca kuṣṭhaṃ kaṣṭaṃ ca rogāñjanayennarāṇām // Rmañj_1.37 //
children.translated_text: destruction of the body, various forms of leprosy, and it generates terrible diseases in humans. (1.37)
<s>Rasamañjarī</s>, Chapter 2.
Now I shall describe the excellent <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion/assimilation) of <s>rasa</s> (mercury);

children.text: athājīrṇam abījaṃ ca sūtakaṃ yastu ghātayet // Rmañj_2.1 //
children.translated_text: he who would kill <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) that is undigested and without seed — (2.1)

children.text: brahmahā sa durācārī mama drohī maheśvari /
children.translated_text: he is a slayer of <s>Brahman</s>, a wicked person, and an offender against me, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>;
therefore, with all effort, one should kill [calcine] <s>rasa</s> (mercury) [only] after [proper] <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion). (2.2)
<s>Pārada-balijāraṇa</s> (mercury digestion by the oblation method):
Having placed water in an earthen pot, [set] a shallow dish on top of it,
equipped with a girdle of powder — one should place inside it — (2.3)
<s>rasa</s> (mercury), and cast the powder of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) on top of it;

children.text: samaṃ bhāgaṃ tato dadyāccharāveṇa pidhāpayet // Rmañj_2.4 //
children.translated_text: then one should give an equal portion, and cover with a shallow dish. (2.4)
The excellent physician should then make a light ash-seal;
with four forest-stones, one should properly perform the <s>puṭa</s> (calcination). (2.5)

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punar gandhaṃ dattvā dattvā bhiṣagvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the excellent physician should again and again add <s>gandha</s> (sulphur),

children.text: samyak kurvīta sūtasya devi ṣaḍguṇajāraṇam // Rmañj_2.6 //
children.translated_text: and properly perform the sixfold <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), O Goddess. (2.6)
<s>Pārada-suvarṇajāraṇa</s> (mercury-gold digestion):

<s>Rasa</s> (mercury) should be ground for three nights with <s>paṭu</s> (salt), <s>śigru</s> (moringa), <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulphate), with <s>rājikā</s> (black mustard) and <s>vyoṣaṇa</s> (the three pungents);

children.text: piṣṭastataḥ svinnatanu suvarṇamukhyānayaṃ khādati sarvadhātūn // Rmañj_2.7 //
children.translated_text: then, being sweated, the thin gold — [or] principally <s>naya</s> (lead) — it devours all metals. (2.7)
Digestion of <s>pārada</s> (mercury):
Alternatively, by the <s>biḍa</s> compound, coated with peacock-bile,

children.text: caret suvarṇaṃ rasarāṭ taptakhalve yathāsukham // Rmañj_2.8 //
children.translated_text: the king of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) should digest gold comfortably in a heated mortar. (2.8)
Powder of burnt conch-shell, soaked with the milk of <s>ravi</s> (<s>arka</s> plant),

children.text: puṭitaṃ śataśo devi praśastaṃ jāraṇaṃ viduḥ // Rmañj_2.9 //
children.translated_text: calcined a hundred times — this, O Goddess, the experts know as the excellent <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion). (2.9)
One should digest gold, mica, and all metals as desired
into <s>sūta</s> (mercury), by various methods, beginning with one-sixty-fourth proportion,

children.text: dvātriṃśat ṣoḍaśāṃśena jārayet kanakaṃ budhaḥ // Rmañj_2.10 //
children.translated_text: the wise one should digest gold in proportions of one-thirty-second and one-sixteenth. (2.10)
Killing of <s>rasa</s> (calcination of mercury):
Two <s>palas</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and half that amount of purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur),
triturated continuously for one day with the juice of <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) — (2.11)

children.text: ruddhvā tadbhūdhare yantre dinaikaṃ mārayet puṭān /
children.translated_text: sealed in a <s>bhūdhara</s> (earthen) apparatus, one should calcine it for one day with <s>puṭas</s>.
Calcination of <s>rasa</s> (method 2):
<s>Pārada</s> (mercury) firmly triturated with the juice of <s>bhujaṅgavallī</s> (snake-creeper) — (2.12)
placed in a sealed crucible of <s>karkoṭī</s> root and clay, in an elephant-<s>puṭa</s> (large calcination),
that <s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash) becomes a carrier of [other] medicines — employ it in all operations. (2.13)
Calcination of <s>rasa</s> (method 3):
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury) should be triturated for three days with the juice of white <s>aṅkola</s> root;
calcined in a blind crucible, the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) attains the state of <s>bhasma</s> (ash). (2.14)
Taking five <s>raktikās</s> (seeds, as a unit of weight) daily with honey and ghee,

children.text: ko vā tasya guṇān vaktuṃ bhuvi śaknoti mānavaḥ // Rmañj_2.15 //
children.translated_text: who among humans on earth is capable of describing its virtues? (2.15)
Preparation of <s>rasasindūra</s> (mercuric compound, method 1):
One <s>pala</s> of purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and an equal measure of pure <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur),
having properly made <s>kajjalī</s> (black mercury-sulphur compound), [triturate] with the water of <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) sprouts — (2.16)
giving three cycles of <s>bhāvanā</s> (levigation), place it in a <s>sthālī</s> (dish);
constructing a <s>kavacīyantra</s> (armored apparatus), fill it with sand. (2.17)
<s>Rasasindūra</s> (mercuric red oxide) is produced, resembling the color of the young morning sun;
with specific <s>anupānas</s> (vehicle substances), it produces various [therapeutic] qualities. (2.18)
<s>Rasasindūra</s> (method 2):
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury) equal [in quantity] to <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), triturated with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (vitex),

children.text: pācito vālukāyantre raktaṃ bhasma prajāyate // Rmañj_2.19 //
children.translated_text: cooked in a sand-bath apparatus — a red <s>bhasma</s> (ash) is produced. (2.19)
<s>Rasasindūra</s>:
Half the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) [amount] of purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), and the essence produced from <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite),
equal to the <s>gandha</s> (sulphur), triturated for a day with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s> (vitex) — (2.20)
one should place it in a glass bottle in a sand-bath apparatus and cook;
or placed in a blind crucible, [cook] for a day in a sand-bath apparatus. (2.21)
A cooked <s>bhasma</s> (ash) is produced, resembling <s>dāḍimī</s> (pomegranate) blossoms.
<s>Rasasindūra</s>:

children.text: pṛthak samaṃ samaṃ kṛtvā pāradaṃ gandhakaṃ tathā // Rmañj_2.22 //
children.translated_text: Having made separately equal portions of <s>pārada</s> (mercury) and <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), (2.22)
and <s>navasāra</s> (ammonium chloride), <s>dhūmasāra</s> (sublimate), and <s>sphaṭikī</s> (alum), [triturate] for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours);
triturating with neem-lemon juice, cook in a glass bottle. (2.23)
Placing a stone tablet at the mouth, apply a seal;

children.text: saptabhir mṛttikāvastraiḥ pṛthak saṃśoṣya veṣṭayet // Rmañj_2.24 //
children.translated_text: with seven layers of clay and cloth, separately drying and wrapping. (2.24)
In a perforated earthen pot, place the bottle;

children.text: pūrayet sikatāpurair ā galaṃ matimān bhiṣak // Rmañj_2.25 //
children.translated_text: the wise physician should fill it with sand up to the neck. (2.25)
Setting fire in a furnace, mild, medium, and strong in succession,

children.text: prajvālya dvādaśaṃ yāmaṃ svāṅgaśītalam uddharet // Rmañj_2.26 //
children.translated_text: having heated for twelve <s>yāmas</s> (36 hours), extract it when self-cooled. (2.26)
Breaking open the pot, discard the <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) that has risen upward;
the <s>rasasindūra</s> (mercuric red oxide) at the bottom — employ it in all operations. (2.27)
<s>Rasasindūra</s>:

children.text: gandhakaṃ dhūma [... au1 Zeichenjh] raṃ ca śuddhasūtaṃ samaṃ samam /
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhaka</s> (sulphur), <s>dhūmasāra</s> (sublimate), and purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in equal parts,
triturate for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) in a mortar and place in a glass bottle. (2.28)
Having sealed it, one should cook it in a sand-bath apparatus (<s>vālukāyantra</s>) for twelve <s>yāmas</s> (watches);

children.text: sphoṭayet svāṅgaśītaṃ tamūrdhvalagnaṃ tu taṃ tyajet /
children.translated_text: one should break it open when cooled naturally; that which adheres to the upper [part] should be discarded;

children.text: adhasthaṃ mṛtasūtaṃ ca sarvayogeṣu yojayet // Rmañj_2.29 //
children.translated_text: the dead mercury (<s>mṛtasūta</s>) at the bottom should be employed in all preparations.
<s>Rasasindūra</s> (Mercury Vermilion)

children.text: bhāgau rasasya traya eva bhāgā gandhasya bhāgaṃ pavanāsanasya /
children.translated_text: Three parts of mercury, one part each of sulphur and <s>pavanāsana</s> (a plant),

children.text: saṃmardya gāḍhaṃ sakalaṃ subhāṇḍe tāṃ kajjalīṃ kācakṛte vidadhyāt // Rmañj_2.30 //
children.translated_text: having ground them all together thoroughly in a good vessel, one should place that <s>kajjalī</s> (black mercury-sulphur mixture) in a glass apparatus.

children.text: saṃveṣṭya mṛtkarpaṭakaiḥ svayaṃ tāṃ mukhe sucūrṇāṃ khaṭikāṃ ca kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: Having wrapped it with clay-cloth covers and placing well-powdered chalk at the mouth,

children.text: kramāgninā trīṇi dināni paktvā tāṃ vālukāyantragatāṃ tataḥ syāt // Rmañj_2.31 //
children.translated_text: cooking it with graduated fire for three days in a sand-bath apparatus — then it is ready.
The ash of the Lord [mercury], red as the <s>bandhūka</s> flower, is to be used in all diseases;

children.text: nijānupānair maraṇaṃ jarāṃ ca nihanti vallakramasevanena // Rmañj_2.32 //
children.translated_text: with appropriate <s>anupānas</s> (vehicles), it destroys death and old age through gradual administration.
<s>Rasasindūra</s> (Mercury Vermilion) [variant preparation]
Mercury from a cooked crucible (<s>pakvamūṣā</s>) and sulphur, placed one above the other,

children.text: tulyaṃ sucūrṇitaṃ kṛtvā kākamācīdravaṃ punaḥ // Rmañj_2.33 //
children.translated_text: having made them into equal fine powder, then [adding] the juice of <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) —

children.text: dvābhyāṃ caturguṇaṃ deyaṃ dravaṃ mūṣāṃ nirudhya ca /
children.translated_text: four times the quantity of the two [mercury and sulphur] should be given as juice; having sealed the crucible,
one should cook it in a sand-bath apparatus with gradually increasing fire for one day;

children.text: āraktaṃ jāyate bhasma sarvayogeṣu yojayet // Rmañj_2.34 //
children.translated_text: a deep-red ash is produced — it should be employed in all preparations.
<s>Rasasindūra</s> (Mercury Vermilion) [third preparation]
The mercury should be carefully sweated with the group [of herbs] beginning with <s>aśvagandhā</s> (Withania somnifera);

children.text: rasatulyaṃ gandhakaṃ ca mardayet kuśalo bhiṣak // Rmañj_2.35 //
children.translated_text: the skilled physician should grind sulphur equal in quantity to the mercury.
When cooked, <s>rasasindūra</s> (mercury vermilion) is produced, resembling the dawn;
it is the best of all mercury preparations, bestowing nourishment, desire, and strength.
This alone is capable of increasing lifespan; nothing else can do so,
even without gold-processing — so have the sages declared.
<s>Rasakarpūra</s> (Mercury Camphor)

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ madhu lākṣātha ūrṇā guñjāyuto rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), honey, lac, wool, mercury combined with <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea) —

children.text: mardayed bhṛṅgajairdrāvairdinaikaṃ vā dhamet punaḥ // Rmañj_2.38 //
children.translated_text: one should grind with juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta alba) for one day, or then blow [with bellows].
When blown, it attains the state of ash, pure and resembling camphor.
<s>Rasakarpūra</s> (Mercury Camphor) [variant preparation]
Chalk, <s>iṣṭikā</s> (brick-powder), <s>gairikā</s> (red ochre), anthill-earth, and <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) in equal parts,
two parts of sulphur and two parts of mercury are prescribed.

children.text: haṇḍikāyāṃ viniḥkṣipya pārśve pārśve ca kharpaṭān // Rmañj_2.40 //
children.translated_text: Having placed [them] in a pot, with cloth-covers on each side,
having burned them and then placing the pot [in fire], one should cook for sixteen <s>praharas</s> (48 hours);
one should collect the dead mercury — pure, resembling camphor.
<s>Rasakarpūra</s> (Mercury Camphor) [third preparation]

children.text: piṣṭaṃ pāṃśupaṭupragāḍhamamalaṃ vajryambunānekaśaḥ sūtaṃ dhātuyutaṃ khaṭīkavalitaṃ taṃ sampuṭe rodhayet /
children.translated_text: Mercury ground repeatedly with <s>vajra</s>-water (diamond-water), very thoroughly until fine and pure like dust, combined with metals and encased in chalk — that should be sealed in a crucible-pair;

children.text: antaḥsthaṃ lavaṇasya tasya ca tale prajvālya vahṇiṃ haṭhāt bhasma grāhyamathendukundadhavalaṃ bhasmoparisthaṃ śanaiḥ // Rmañj_2.42 //
children.translated_text: with salt placed inside at its base, having forcefully ignited fire — the ash should be collected, white as moon, <s>kunda</s> (jasmine), slowly from above the ash.

body.translated_text: Having wrapped it in <s>kalka</s> (paste) etc., one should swallow it with a snack as vehicle.

children.text: tadvalladvitayaṃ lavaṅgasahitaṃ prātaḥ prabhuktaṃ nṛṇām ūrdhvaṃ recayati dviyāmamasakṛtpeyaṃ jalaṃ śītalam /
children.translated_text: Two <s>vallas</s> (doses) of that, along with cloves, taken in the morning by people, causes purging upward after two <s>yāmas</s> (watches); cold water should be drunk repeatedly;

children.text: etaddhanti ca vatsarāvadhi viṣaṃ ṣāṇmāsikaṃ māsikaṃ śailotthaṃ garalaṃ mṛgendrakuṭilodbhūtaṃ ca tātkālikam // Rmañj_2.43 //
children.translated_text: this destroys poison [accumulated] over a year, over six months, over one month, mineral poison, and poison arising from the curve of a lion [bite] — even immediately.
<s>Rasamūrchanā</s> (Mercury Swooning/Fainting)
One should grind mercury with <s>meghanāda</s> (a plant), <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), and garlic;

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu tadgolaṃ hiṅgunā veṣṭayedbahiḥ // Rmañj_2.44 //
children.translated_text: that pill, ground until dissolved, should be wrapped externally with <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida).
One should cook it placed in a salt-apparatus (<s>lavaṇayantra</s>) for one day with fierce fire;

children.text: ūrdhvalagnaṃ samādāya dṛḍhaṃ vastreṇa veṣṭayet // Rmañj_2.45 //
children.translated_text: taking that which adheres to the upper part, one should wrap it tightly with cloth.

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ tulyaṃ dattvā saumyānale pacet /
children.translated_text: Placing equal sulphur above and below, one should cook in gentle fire;

children.text: jīrṇe gandhe punardeyaṃ ṣaḍbhir vāraiḥ samaṃ samam // Rmañj_2.46 //
children.translated_text: when the sulphur is absorbed, more should be given — six times, in equal amounts each time.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇe gandhake jīrṇe mūrchito rogahā bhavet /
children.translated_text: When sixfold sulphur has been absorbed, the swooned [mercury] becomes a disease-destroyer.
<s>Rasamūrchanā</s> (Mercury Swooning) [variant preparation]
In an iron vessel or copper one, one <s>pala</s> (unit of weight) of purified sulphur —
when it is melted on gentle fire, three <s>palas</s> of purified mercury

children.text: kṣiptvātha cālayet kiṃcillohadarvyā punaḥ punaḥ // Rmañj_2.48 //
children.translated_text: should be thrown in, and then it should be stirred slightly with an iron ladle, again and again.
Cow-dung and a plantain leaf [should be placed] on top, and it should be poured out.

children.text: ityevaṃ gandhabaddhaṃ ca sarvarogeṣu yojayet // Rmañj_2.49 //
children.translated_text: Thus the sulphur-bound [mercury] should be employed in all diseases.
Killed [mercury] is for perfecting the body; swooned [mercury] is for destroying diseases;
mercury-ash in some diseases is for the body, swooned [mercury] in others;

children.text: baddho dvābhyāṃ prayuñjīta śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā // Rmañj_2.50 //
children.translated_text: bound [mercury] should be employed for both, through procedures prescribed in the <s>śāstras</s>.
Characteristics of Bound Mercury (<s>Baddha Pārada</s>)

children.text: akṣayī ca laghurdrāvī tejasvī nirmalo guruḥ /
children.translated_text: Imperishable, light, fluid, lustrous, pure, and heavy —
splitting and returning again — these are the characteristics of bound mercury.
Characteristics of Swooned Mercury (<s>Mūrchita Pārada</s>)
When mercury, having abandoned its dense fluidity,

children.text: dṛśyate'sau tadā jñeyo mūrchitaḥ sutarāṃ budhaiḥ // Rmañj_2.52 //
children.translated_text: appears like lampblack (<s>kajjala</s>) — then the wise should know it as swooned.
Characteristics of Dead Mercury (<s>Mṛta Pārada</s>)

children.text: ārdratvaṃ ca ghanatvaṃ ca cāpalyaṃ gurutaijasam /
children.translated_text: Moistness, density, fluidity, heaviness, and luster —

children.text: yasyaitāni na dṛśyante taṃ vidyānmṛtasūtakam // Rmañj_2.53 //
children.translated_text: that in which these are not seen should be known as dead mercury.
Seedless Bound Mercury (<s>Nirbīja Baddha Pārada</s>)
Mercury that has absorbed a quarter-part of gold, made into paste by the addition of sulphur,
calcined gradually with equal parts of sulphur — it is called seedless, the destroyer of all diseases.
Seeded Bound Mercury (<s>Sabīja Baddha Pārada</s>)
This [mercury], processed with seed-substances — the essence of mica, gold, <s>tārā</s> (silver), and <s>sūryakānta</s> and <s>arkakānta</s> (sun-stone and solar gems) —
then with sixfold sulphur powder — even seeded-bound, it has superior potency.
In taste, potency, and post-digestive effect, one should know mercury to be nectar-like;

children.text: sevito'sau sadā dehe roganāśāya kalpate // Rmañj_2.56 //
children.translated_text: constantly consumed, it serves to destroy diseases of the body.
The Eight K-substances (<s>Kakārāṣṭaka</s>)
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash-gourd), <s>karkaṭī</s> (cucumber), <s>kaliṅga</s> (watermelon), <s>kāravellaka</s> (bitter gourd),

children.text: kusumbhikaṃ ca karkoṭīṃ kadalīṃ kākamācikām // Rmañj_2.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>kusumbhika</s> (safflower), <s>karkoṭī</s> (a kind of cucumber), <s>kadalī</s> (plantain), and <s>kākamācikā</s> (black nightshade) —
these eight K-substances should be avoided by one who consumes mercury.

children.text: hitaṃ mudgāmbudugdhājyaṃ śālyannaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ // Rmañj_2.58 //
children.translated_text: Beneficial are: <s>mudga</s> (green gram), water, milk, ghee, and <s>śāli</s> rice-food especially.
The greens of <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa), <s>meghanāda</s>, and <s>cillikā</s>,

children.text: saindhavaṃ nāgaraṃ mustaṃ padmamūlāni bhakṣayet // Rmañj_2.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), dry ginger, <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus rotundus), and lotus-roots should be eaten.

children.text: abhyaṅgaṃ maithunaṃ snānaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ ca sukhāmbunā /
children.translated_text: Oil massage, sexual intercourse, and bathing — as desired, with pleasant water;
one should enjoy a beloved wife endowed with beauty and youth, who is agreeable.

children.text: buddhiḥ prajñā balaṃ kāntiḥ prabhā caivaṃ vayastathā /
children.translated_text: Intelligence, wisdom, strength, luster, radiance, and vitality —

children.text: vardhante sarva evaite rasasevāvidhau nṛṇām // Rmañj_2.61 //
children.translated_text: all of these increase in people following the regimen of mercury consumption.

children.text: yasya rogasya yo yogastenaiva saha yojayet /
children.translated_text: Whatever preparation is appropriate for a given disease, with that very [preparation] should it be employed;
<s>Rasendra</s> (Lord Mercury) destroys the diseases of humans, elephants, and horses.
The Subsidiary Minerals (<s>Uparasāḥ</s>)
<s>Gandhaka</s> (sulphur), <s>vajra</s> (diamond), <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>gagana</s> (talc), <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), <s>śilā</s> (realgar),

children.text: kharparaṃ śikhitutthaṃ ca vimalā hemamākṣikam // Rmañj_3.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>kharpara</s> (calamine), <s>śikhituttha</s> (blue vitriol), <s>vimalā</s>, and <s>hemamākṣika</s> (iron pyrite) —
<s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> (magnetite), <s>varāṭā</s> (cowry), <s>añjana</s> (collyrium), <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar),

children.text: kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ śaṃkhabhūnāgaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tu śilājatu // Rmañj_3.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>śaṅkha</s> (conch), <s>bhūnāga</s> (earthworm), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>śilājatu</s> (bitumen) —

children.text: ete uparasāḥ proktāḥ śodhyā drāvyāśca mārayet /
children.translated_text: these are declared as subsidiary minerals; they should be purified, rendered fluid, and killed.
<s>Gandhaka</s> (Sulphur)

children.text: tatrādau gandhakotpattiṃ śodhanaṃ tvatha kathyate // Rmañj_3.3 //
children.translated_text: First, the origin of sulphur and then its purification are described.

children.text: śvetadvīpe purā devyāḥ krīḍantyāḥ prasṛtaṃ rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the white island (<s>Śvetadvīpa</s>), long ago, the menstrual discharge (<s>rajas</s>) that flowed from the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) while she was playing,

children.text: kṣīrārṇave tu snātāyā dukūlaṃ rajasānvitam // Rmañj_3.4 //
children.translated_text: and the garment stained with menstrual blood when she bathed in the milk-ocean —

children.text: dhautaṃ yat salile tasmin gandhavadgandhakaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: that which was washed in that water, being fragrant, is known as <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur, lit. "fragrant substance").
Sulphur is declared to be fourfold: red, yellow, white, and black.
Red is prescribed for gold-making operations; yellow for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation);

children.text: vraṇādilepane śvetaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kṛṣṇastu durlabhaḥ // Rmañj_3.6 //
children.translated_text: white for application on wounds etc.; black is the best but rare.

children.text: aśuddhagandhaḥ kurute'tikuṣṭhaṃ tāpaṃ bhramaṃ pittarujaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: Unpurified sulphur produces severe leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), causes burning, dizziness, and ailments of <s>pitta</s>;

children.text: rūpaṃ sukhaṃ vīryabalaṃ nihanti tasmāt suśuddhaṃ viniyojanīyam // Rmañj_3.7 //
children.translated_text: it destroys beauty, comfort, virility, and strength — therefore it should be used only when well purified.
Purification of Sulphur (method 1)

children.text: sājyabhāṇḍe payaḥ kṣiptvā mukhaṃ vastreṇa bandhayet /
children.translated_text: Having placed milk in a vessel smeared with ghee, one should tie the mouth with cloth;
having placed sulphur on its back [upper surface], one should cover it with a saucer.

children.text: bhāṇḍaṃ nikṣipya bhūmyāṃ tadūrdhvaṃ deyaṃ puṭaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: Placing that vessel on the ground, a light calcination (<s>puṭa</s>) should be given from above;

children.text: tataḥ kṣīreṇa gandhaṃ ca śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet // Rmañj_3.9 //
children.translated_text: then the sulphur [fallen into the] milk is purified — it should be employed in preparations.
Purification of Sulphur (method 2)
The knower of truth should purify sulphur in milk by means of a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>);

children.text: tena śuddho bhavatyeṣa dhātūṇāṃ prāṇamūrchakaḥ // Rmañj_3.10 //
children.translated_text: thus purified, it becomes the life-swooner of metals.
Purification of Sulphur (method 3)
One should melt sulphur mixed with ghee on fire using an iron ladle;

children.text: ekībhūtaṃ tato gandhaṃ dugdhamadhye parikṣipet // Rmañj_3.11 //
children.translated_text: when the sulphur has become unified, one should cast it into the midst of milk.
Thereby the sulphur becomes purified — it should be employed in all preparations.
When purified, the king of mercury [i.e., sulphur as mercury's partner] removes old age, death, and disease;

children.text: agnisaṃdīpanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vīryavṛddhiṃ karoti ca // Rmañj_3.12 //
children.translated_text: it is excellent for kindling the digestive fire and increases virility.
Sulphur Oil (<s>Gandhakataila</s>)
A cloth should be smeared seven times with the milk of <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) and <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia);

children.text: gandhakaṃ navanītena piṣṭvā vastraṃ lipettu tat // Rmañj_3.13 //
children.translated_text: having ground sulphur with fresh butter, that cloth should be smeared with it.

body.translated_text: That wick, when lit and held by bamboo [tongs], should be held face-down.

children.text: tailaṃ patatyadho bhāṇḍe grāhyaṃ yogeṣu yojayet /
children.translated_text: Oil drips down into a vessel below — it should be collected and employed in preparations.

children.text: agnisaṃdīpanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vīryavṛddhiṃ karoti ca // Rmañj_3.15 //
children.translated_text: It is excellent for kindling the digestive fire and increases virility.
<s>Hīraka</s> (Diamond)
White, yellow, red, and black — these are the types of diamond, [belonging to] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and other [castes].

children.text: puṃstrīnapuṃsakaṃ ceti lakṣaṇena tu lakṣayet // Rmañj_3.16 //
children.translated_text: Male, female, and neuter — these should be identified by their characteristics.
Round, full-faceted, lustrous, and large —
those are declared as male, devoid of lines and spots.
Those endowed with lines and spots, hexagonal — these are considered female;
triangular and elongated like a leaf — these should be known as neuter.
Among all, the males are best — they pierce and bind mercury;
female diamond is for perfecting the body; neuter is for transmutation.
The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [diamond] is prescribed for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation); the <s>Kṣatriya</s> for disease-destruction;
the <s>Vaiśya</s>-type for alchemical operations etc.; and the fourth [<s>Śūdra</s>-type] for arresting aging.

children.text: strī tu striye pradātavyā klībe klībaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Female [diamond] should be given to a woman, and neuter to a eunuch;

children.text: sarveṣāṃ sarvadā yojyāḥ puruṣā balavattarāḥ // Rmañj_3.21 //
children.translated_text: male [diamonds], being more powerful, should be employed for all, always.
Pallor (<s>pāṇḍuroga</s>), side-pain, leukoderma (<s>kilāsa</s>), continuous burning,

children.text: rogānīkaṃ gurutvaṃ ca dhatte vajram aśodhitam // Rmañj_3.22 //
children.translated_text: a host of diseases, and heaviness — unpurified diamond produces [these].
Purification of Diamond (method 1)
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond) placed in the bulb of <s>vyāghrī</s> (Solanum), cooked in a swing-apparatus

children.text: saptāhaṃ kodravakvāthe kaulatthe vimalaṃ bhavet // Rmañj_3.23 //
children.translated_text: for seven days in a decoction of <s>kodrava</s> (millet) and <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram) — it becomes pure.
Purification of Diamond (method 2)

children.text: vyāghrīkandagataṃ vajraṃ mṛdā liptaṃ puṭe pacet /
children.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s> placed in the bulb of <s>vyāghrī</s>, smeared with clay, should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> (calcination);
after one day and night, having taken it out, one should sprinkle it with horse urine;

children.text: vajrīkṣīreṇa vā siñcet kuliśaṃ vimalaṃ bhavet // Rmañj_3.24 //
children.translated_text: or one should sprinkle it with the milk of <s>vajrī</s> (Euphorbia) — the diamond becomes pure.
Killing of Diamond (method 1)
Having taken the root of three-year-old cotton plant, one should grind it
with the juice of three-year-old <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel vine).
Having placed the diamond in that ball and sealed it, one should cook in an elephant-<s>puṭa</s> (large calcination);

children.text: evaṃ saptapuṭaṃ kṛtvā kuliśaṃ mriyate dhruvam // Rmañj_3.26 //
children.translated_text: having done seven such calcinations, the diamond certainly dies.
Killing of Diamond (method 2)

children.text: kāṃsyapātre tu bhekasya mūtre vajraṃ subhāvayet /
children.translated_text: In a bronze vessel, one should soak the diamond well in frog's urine;

children.text: triḥ saptakṛtvaḥ saṃtaptaṃ vajrameva mṛtaṃ bhavet // Rmañj_3.27 //
children.translated_text: quenched twenty-one times — the diamond itself becomes dead.
Killing of Diamond (method 3)
Quenched twenty-one times, one should sprinkle it with donkey's urine;

children.text: matkuṇaistālakaṃ piṣṭvā tadgole kuliśaṃ kṣipet // Rmañj_3.28 //
children.translated_text: having ground <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) with bedbugs, the diamond should be placed in that ball.
Blown [with bellows] and sprinkled with horse's urine in the manner described before —
It becomes <s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash); consuming it makes the body like <s>vajra</s> (diamond). // Rmañj_3.29 //
It promotes longevity, generates happiness, bestows strength and beauty,
destroys diseases and removes death — <s>vajra-bhasma</s> (diamond ash) is indeed efficacious. // Rmañj_3.30 //
<Section: <s>Vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline)>
Eight-edged, eight-faced, six-cornered, smooth, and heavy,
endowed with pure mixed colours — this is called <s>vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline). // Rmañj_3.31 //
White, red, yellow, blue, pigeon-coloured,

children.text: śyāmalaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaśca karburaścāṣṭadhā hi saḥ // Rmañj_3.32 //
children.translated_text: dark, black, and variegated — it is thus of eight kinds. // Rmañj_3.32 //
<Section: Purification of <s>Vaikrānta</s>>
<s>Vaikrānta</s> is purified like <s>vajra</s> (diamond); it is heated and [quenched] in horse urine,

children.text: hitaṃ tadbhasma saṃyojyaṃ vajrasthāne vicakṣaṇaiḥ // Rmañj_3.33 //
children.translated_text: its <s>bhasma</s> (ash) should be employed by the wise in place of <s>vajra</s>. // Rmañj_3.33 //
It bestows longevity, binds all [metals], is a great aphrodisiac, grants wisdom, uproots all diseases entirely,

children.text: dīptāgnikṛt pavisamānaguṇas tarasvī vaikrāntakaḥ khalu vapurbalalohakārī // Rmañj_3.34 //
children.translated_text: kindles the digestive fire, possesses qualities equal to <s>Pavi</s> (thunderbolt), is potent — <s>vaikrāntaka</s> indeed makes the body strong as iron. // Rmañj_3.34 //
<Section: Extraction of <s>Vaikrānta-sattva</s> (essence)>
<s>Vaikrānta</s> should be ground with <s>vajra-kanda</s> (diamond-bulb) in <s>vajra</s>-water,

children.text: māhiṣaṃ navanītaṃ ca sakṣaudraṃ piṇḍitaṃ tataḥ // Rmañj_3.35 //
children.translated_text: then mixed with buffalo butter and honey into a ball. // Rmañj_3.35 //
<Section: <s>Abhraka</s> (mica)>
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica) is of four kinds: <s>pināka</s>, <s>dardura</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>vajra</s>,

children.text: dhmātaṃ vahṇau dalacayaṃ pinākaṃ visṛjatyalam // Rmañj_3.36 //
children.translated_text: when heated in fire, the <s>pināka</s> variety releases many flakes. // Rmañj_3.36 //

body.translated_text: After drying, one should smelt it; the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) becomes like an <s>Indragopa</s> (cochineal insect, i.e. red).

children.translated_text: The <s>dardura</s> type hisses like a serpent and [sounds] like a frog,

children.text: caturthaṃ ca varaṃ jñeyaṃ na cāgnau vikṛtiṃ vrajet // Rmañj_3.37 //
children.translated_text: the fourth (<s>vajra</s>) is known as the best, and it does not undergo change in fire. // Rmañj_3.37 //
Therefore, <s>vajra-abhraka</s> (diamond-mica) should be chosen; it conquers disease, old age, and death.
Impure <s>abhraka</s> destroys lifespan and increases <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm). // Rmañj_3.38 //
Unprocessed [mica] cuts the limbs, promotes sluggish digestion and worms,
therefore purified <s>abhraka</s> should be used, which destroys sluggish digestion and worms. // Rmañj_3.39 //
<Section: <s>Dhānyābhraka</s> (grain-mica)>
One part of rice mixed with <s>abhraka</s>, tied in a cloth,

children.text: trirātraṃ sthāpayennīre tat klinnaṃ mardayed dṛḍham // Rmañj_3.40 //
children.translated_text: should be placed in water for three nights; the soaked [mass] should be firmly ground. // Rmañj_3.40 //
That which filters through the cloth, fine and free of sand,
is called <s>dhānyābhraka</s> (grain-mica) by the wise, for the perfection of the body. // Rmañj_3.41 //
<Section: Preparation of <s>Dhānyābhraka</s>>
One should heat <s>vajra-abhraka</s> in fire, then sprinkle it with milk,
splitting its leaves, then with the juices of <s>Meghanāda</s> and sour substances,
one should soak it for eight <s>yāmas</s> (a quarter of a day); thus the wise one should prepare <s>dhānyābhraka</s>. // Rmañj_3.42 //
<Section: <s>Dhānyābhraka</s> (alternative method)>
Alternatively, one should immerse heated <s>abhraka</s> in a decoction of <s>badarī</s> (jujube),

children.text: marditaṃ pāṇinā śuṣkaṃ dhānyābhrād atiricyate // Rmañj_3.43 //
children.translated_text: ground by hand and dried, it surpasses [regular] <s>dhānyābhraka</s>. // Rmañj_3.43 //

children.text: dhānyābhrakasya bhāgaikaṃ dvau bhāgau ṭaṃkaṇasya ca // Rmañj_3.44 //
children.translated_text: One part of <s>dhānyābhraka</s> and two parts of <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s> (borax), // Rmañj_3.44 //
ground together, sealed in a blind crucible, and cooked with intense fire;
the naturally cooled powder should be used for all diseases. // Rmañj_3.45 //
<Section: Calcination of <s>Abhraka</s> (method 1)>
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s> should be firmly ground in <s>arka</s>-milk (milkweed latex) for a day,

children.text: veṣṭayed bhānupatraiśca cakrākāraṃ tu kārayet // Rmañj_3.46 //
children.translated_text: wrapped in <s>arka</s>-leaves and made into a disc shape. // Rmañj_3.46 //

children.text: kuñjarākhye puṭe pācyaṃ saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: It should be heated in the <s>kuñjara-puṭa</s> (elephant-grade furnace) seven times, again and again,
then similarly given three more firings with decoctions of banyan aerial roots. // Rmañj_3.47 //
It will certainly be calcined; it should be used for all diseases.
<Section: Calcination of <s>Abhraka</s> (method 2)>
Taking <s>dhānyābhraka</s>, [give] three firings with decoctions of <s>musta</s> (nutgrass), // Rmañj_3.48 //
similarly with juices of <s>Punarnava</s> (Boerhavia diffusa), <s>Kāsamarda</s> (Senna),
combined with <s>Nāgavallī</s> (betel) juices and <s>arka</s>-milk, each separately. // Rmañj_3.49 //
Grinding day by day with decoctions made from banyan aerial roots,

children.text: dattvā puṭatrayaṃ paścāt tripuṭaṃ muśalījalaiḥ // Rmañj_3.50 //
children.translated_text: then giving three firings, afterwards three firings with <s>Muśalī</s> (Curculigo) juices, // Rmañj_3.50 //
three times with <s>Gokṣura</s> (Tribulus) decoction, three firings with <s>Vānarī</s> juices,
it should be fired three times with <s>Mocā</s> (plantain) stem juices and <s>Kokilākṣa</s> (Asteracantha) // Rmañj_3.51 //

children.text: rasaiḥ puṭettato dhenuḥ kṣārodakaṃ puṭaṃ muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: juices; then [fire with] cow's milk, alkaline water, firing repeatedly,

children.text: dadhnā ghṛtena madhunā svacchayā sitayā tathā // Rmañj_3.52 //
children.translated_text: with curd, ghee, honey, and pure sugar likewise. // Rmañj_3.52 //
One should give one firing with each — thus the death (calcination) of <s>abhraka</s> is accomplished.
<s>Vyoma</s> (mica) becomes destroyer of all diseases and a <s>yogavāhaka</s> (carrier of medicinal efficacy). // Rmañj_3.53 //
It destroys the pride and arrogance of women, is praised for those seeking virility,
it is aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, increases <s>śukra</s> (semen), and bestows progeny. // Rmañj_3.54 //
<Section: Calcination of <s>Abhraka</s> (method 3)>
The three milks (cow, buffalo, goat), <s>Kumārī</s> (aloe) juice, <s>Gaṅgā</s>-leaf (Oxalis), human urine,
banyan sprouts, goat's blood — with these, <s>abhraka</s> well ground, // Rmañj_3.55 //
fired a hundred times, becomes <s>bhasma</s> (ash) like a ruby,

children.text: niścandrakaṃ bhaved vyoma śuddhadeho rasāyanam // Rmañj_3.56 //
children.translated_text: free of specks — <s>vyoma</s> (mica) with a purified body becomes a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // Rmañj_3.56 //

children.text: niścandramāritaṃ vyoma rūpaṃ vīryaṃ dṛḍhāṃ tanum /
children.translated_text: Speck-free calcined <s>vyoma</s> bestows beauty, vigour, and a firm body,
it destroys death and the multitude of old age and diseases. // Rmañj_3.57 //
<Section: Extraction of <s>Abhraka-sattva</s> (mica essence)>

children.text: bhāvitaṃ cūrṇitaṃ tvabhraṃ dinaikaṃ kāñjikena ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Abhraka</s>, powdered and soaked for one day in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel),
should be mixed with juices of plantain, <s>Sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam), and radish. // Rmañj_3.58 //
A quarter part of <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s> (borax) and an equal amount of small fish,
mixed with buffalo dung, one should make a ball. // Rmañj_3.59 //
Smelted with fierce fire, it releases a lustrous <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence);
the wise one who consumes the <s>sattva</s>, properly purified, attains arrest of aging. // Rmañj_3.60 //
<Section: Liquefaction of <s>Abhraka</s>>
Ground with the exudate of <s>Agasti</s> (Sesbania) flowers, [placed] inside an <s>Sūraṇa</s> (yam),
kept in a cowshed, the <s>abhraka</s> becomes lustrous and water-like. // Rmañj_3.61 //
<Section: <s>Sattva-pātana</s> (essence extraction — general method)>
<s>Guḍa</s> (jaggery), then <s>lākṣā</s> (lac), <s>piṇyāka</s> (oil cake), <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s> (borax),
wool, <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal resin), together with small fish, // Rmañj_3.62 //

children.text: etat sarvaṃ tu saṃcūrṇaṃ chāgīdugdhena piṇḍikām /
children.translated_text: all this powdered, made into a ball with goat's milk,

children.text: kṛtvā dhmātā kharāṅgāraiḥ sarvasattvāni pātayet // Rmañj_3.63 //
children.translated_text: smelted with hard charcoal — one can extract the <s>sattva</s> (essence) of all [minerals]. // Rmañj_3.63 //
Stones, clays, and the like, and all metals —

children.text: anyāni yānyasādhyāni vyomasattvasya kā kathā // Rmañj_3.64 //
children.translated_text: even those otherwise intractable — what need be said of the <s>sattva</s> of mica? // Rmañj_3.64 //
Whatever has the nature of a subsidiary mineral, its <s>sattva</s> should be combined with mercury;
this should be done for enhancing its qualities, if one desires mastery of <s>rasa</s> (mercury/alchemy). // Rmañj_3.65 //
<Section: Extraction of <s>Bhūnāga-sattva</s> (earthworm essence)>
Taking fresh <s>bhūnāga</s> (earthworms), the wise one should feed them to a peacock,

children.text: athavā kukkuṭaṃ vīraṃ kṛtvā mandiramāśritam // Rmañj_3.66 //
children.translated_text: or to a heroic rooster, keeping it sheltered. // Rmañj_3.66 //

children.text: malaṃ mūtraṃ gṛhītvā ca saṃtyajya prathamāṃśakam /
children.translated_text: Taking the excrement and urine, discarding the first portion,
mixing with milk, honey, and ghee, one should smelt carefully for the <s>sattva</s>. // Rmañj_3.67 //
They release a <s>sattva</s> like copper; drinking the water [infused with] its seal,
all <s>jaṅgama</s> (animal-origin) poisons are destroyed, without doubt. // Rmañj_3.68 //
<Section: Defects of impure <s>Haritāla</s> (orpiment)>
Impure <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) destroys lifespan, produces <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>vāta</s> (wind), and urinary disorders,
causes vomiting, boils, and contraction of limbs; therefore it should be purified. // Rmañj_3.69 //
<Section: <s>Haritāla</s> (orpiment)>
Purified <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), steamed in <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd) juice, then

children.text: cūrṇodake pṛthaktaile bhasmībhūto na doṣakṛt // Rmañj_3.70 //
children.translated_text: in lime-water and separately in oil — when reduced to ash, it causes no defects. // Rmañj_3.70 //
<s>Tālaka</s> removes diseases such as <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), death, and pain;

children.text: saṃśuddhaḥ kāntivīryaṃ ca kurute hyāyurvardhanam // Rmañj_3.71 //
children.translated_text: when properly purified, it bestows lustre, vigour, and indeed prolongs life. // Rmañj_3.71 //
<Section: Calcination of <s>Haritāla</s>>
One <s>pala</s> (measure) of purified <s>tāla</s>, ground with <s>Kumārī</s> (aloe) juice,
placed in a saucer-sealed vessel, should be cooked for twelve <s>yāmas</s> (three days). // Rmañj_3.72 //

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ samādāya tālakaṃ tu mṛtaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: When naturally cooled, the <s>tālaka</s> will be calcined;

children.text: galatkuṣṭhaṃ hareccaiva tālakaṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ // Rmañj_3.73 //
children.translated_text: it cures <s>galatkuṣṭha</s> (leprosy with falling flesh), without doubt. // Rmañj_3.73 //
<Section: Purification of <s>Manaḥśilā</s> (realgar)>
Soaked seven times in water of <s>Agasti</s> (Sesbania) leaves,
or with <s>Śṛṅgavera</s> (ginger) juices, <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) is purified. // Rmañj_3.74 //
<Section: Properties of <s>Manaḥśilā</s>>

children.text: kaṭuḥ snigdhā śilā tiktā kaphaghnī lekhanī parā /
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s> is pungent, unctuous, bitter, destroys <s>kapha</s>, and is an excellent scraping agent;
it cures affliction by spirits and <s>āmaya</s> (disease), and is beneficial in removing cough and asthma. // Rmañj_3.75 //
<Section: Purification of <s>Rasaka</s> (calamine/zinc ore)>
<s>Rasaka</s> should be cooked in human urine and donkey urine for seven days,

children.text: dolāyantrena saṃśodhya tataḥ kāryeṣu yojayet // Rmañj_3.76 //
children.translated_text: purified in a <s>dolā-yantra</s> (swing apparatus), then employed in procedures. // Rmañj_3.76 //
<Section: Purification of <s>Tuttha</s> (blue vitriol/copper sulphate)>
<s>Tuttha</s> mixed equally with camel dung, with honey and <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s> (borax), by the physician,
fired three times, becomes purified and free of vomiting and dizziness [side-effects]. // Rmañj_3.77 //
<Section: Properties of <s>Tuttha</s>>

children.text: tutthakaṃ kaṭu sakṣāraṃ kaṣāyaṃ viśadaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: <s>Tutthaka</s> (blue vitriol) is pungent, alkaline, astringent, clear, and light;
it is a scraping agent, purgative, beneficial for the eyes, and removes itching, worms, and poison. // Rmañj_3.78 //
<Section: <s>Vimala</s> (iron pyrite)>
Steamed in the juice of <s>Jambīra</s> (citron), or in <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s> juice,

children.text: rambhātoyena vā pācyaṃ ghasraṃ vimalaśuddhaye // Rmañj_3.79 //
children.translated_text: or cooked in plantain water for a day — for the purification of <s>Vimala</s>. // Rmañj_3.79 //
<Section: Purification of <s>Mākṣika</s> (chalcopyrite/copper pyrite)>
One part of <s>Sindhu-born</s> (rock salt) and three parts of <s>mākṣika</s> (chalcopyrite),

children.text: kṛtvā tadāyase pātre lohadarvyātha cālayet // Rmañj_3.80 //
children.translated_text: placed in an iron vessel, should be stirred with an iron ladle. // Rmañj_3.80 //
Cook on gentle fire until it becomes <s>sindūra</s>-coloured (vermilion);

children.text: subhadraṃ mākṣikaṃ vidyāt sarvayogeṣu yojayet // Rmañj_3.81 //
children.translated_text: know that <s>mākṣika</s> is then well-purified; it should be used in all formulations. // Rmañj_3.81 //
<Section: Calcination of <s>Mākṣika</s>>
Adding one-fourth part of <s>gandha</s> (sulphur) to <s>mākṣika</s>, one should grind it

children.text: ūrubūkasya tailena tataḥ kāryā sucakrikā // Rmañj_3.82 //
children.translated_text: with the oil of <s>Ūrubūka</s> (castor); then make a proper disc. // Rmañj_3.82 //
Placing it in a saucer-sealed vessel, fire it with the <s>gaja-puṭa</s> (elephant-grade furnace);

children.text: sindūrābhaṃ bhaved bhasma mākṣikasya na saṃśayaḥ // Rmañj_3.83 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bhasma</s> of <s>mākṣika</s> becomes <s>sindūra</s>-coloured (vermilion), without doubt. // Rmañj_3.83 //
<Section: Properties of <s>Mākṣika</s>>
<s>Mākṣika</s> is bitter and sweet, cures urinary disorders, hemorrhoids, consumption, and skin diseases;
it removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is strengthening, a <s>yogavāhi</s> (carrier of medicinal efficacy), and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // Rmañj_3.84 //

children.text: sakṛd bhṛṅgāmbunā svinnaṃ kāsīsaṃ nirmalaṃ bhavet // Rmañj_3.85 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāsīsa</s> steamed once in <s>Bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) water becomes purified. // Rmañj_3.85 //
<Section: Properties of <s>Kāsīsa</s>>
<s>Kāsīsa</s> is cooling, unctuous; when steamed, it removes eye diseases,
alleviates <s>pitta</s> and epilepsy, and acts as a quality-enhancing agent like mercury. // Rmañj_3.86 //
<Section: <s>Kānta-pāṣāṇa</s> (lodestone/magnetite)>
Salts and alkalis should be placed in <s>Śobhāñjana</s> (Moringa) juice,

children.text: amlavargayute cādau dinam ardhaṃ vibhāvayet // Rmañj_3.87 //
children.translated_text: combined with the sour group, and heated for half a day first. // Rmañj_3.87 //
With those liquids, in a <s>dolā-yantra</s> (swing apparatus), the wise one should cook it for a day;
for the purification of <s>kānta-pāṣāṇa</s> (lodestone), one should then proceed with mercury operations. // Rmañj_3.88 //
<Section: <s>Varāṭikā</s> (cowrie shells)>
Yellowish, knotted on the back, elongated and oval — these are <s>varāṭikās</s> (cowrie shells);
those weighing one and a half <s>niṣka</s> (a weight measure) are the best, those of one <s>niṣka</s> are middling, // Rmañj_3.89 //
those weighing three-quarters of a <s>niṣka</s> are declared the lowest;
as specified by the <s>rasa-vaidya</s> (alchemist-physician), they are designated as <s>cara</s> and <s>acara</s> (mobile and immobile). // Rmañj_3.90 //
<Section: Purification of <s>Varāṭā</s> (cowrie)>
<s>Varāṭā</s> (cowrie) steamed in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) attains purity.
<Section: Properties of <s>Varāṭā</s>>
It cures <s>pariṇāma</s>-colic and other abdominal pains, destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> (sprue) and consumption, // Rmañj_3.91 //
it is pungent, hot, appetizing, aphrodisiac, good for the eyes, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>;
it is recommended in the <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) of mercury and is praised among <s>viḍa</s>-substances (auxiliary agents). // Rmañj_3.92 //
<Section: Purification of <s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar)>
<s>Darada</s> (cinnabar) soaked in ewe's milk and the sour group,
seven times with care, certainly attains purity. // Rmañj_3.93 //
<Section: Properties of <s>Hiṅgula</s>>
<s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) is bitter, hot, and divine, born of mercury and sulphur;
it cures urinary disorders and skin diseases, is tasty, strengthening, and kindles intellect and digestion. // Rmañj_3.94 //
<Section: Purification of <s>Śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch/shilajit)>
<s>Śilājatu</s> (shilajit), ground with cow's milk, <s>Triphalā</s>, and <s>Bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) juices,
[kept] for one day in an iron vessel, attains purity without doubt. // Rmañj_3.95 //
<Section: Properties of <s>Śilājatu</s>>
<s>Śilājatu</s> is bitter, pungent, hot, and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative);
it destroys consumption, wasting, abdominal diseases, and hemorrhoids, and conquers bladder ailments. // Rmañj_3.96 //

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṃkaṇaṃ śaṃkhaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ gairikaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sauvīra</s> (antimony ore), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>śaṅkha</s> (conch shell), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (a mineral), and <s>gairika</s> (red ochre) —
these should be purified like <s>varāṭā</s> (cowrie shells) and become free from defects. // Rmañj_3.97 //
<Purification of gems>
<s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby) is purified by acid, and <s>mauktika</s> (pearl) by <s>jayantī</s> (a plant);
<s>Vidruma</s> (coral) by the group of alkalis, and <s>tārkṣya</s> (emerald) by cow's milk and such. // Rmañj_3.98 //
<s>Puṣparāga</s> (topaz) by fermented preparations combined with decoction of <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram);

children.text: taṇḍulīyajalair vajraṃ nīlaṃ nīlīrasena ca // Rmañj_3.99 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s> (diamond) by the juice of <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (amaranth), and <s>nīla</s> (sapphire) by the juice of indigo. // Rmañj_3.99 //
<s>Gomeda</s> (hessonite) by <s>rocanā</s> (ox-bile pigment), and <s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's eye) by <s>triphalā</s> (three-fruit) water;
ground with the juice of <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) together with <s>śilā</s> (orpiment), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), and <s>tālaka</s> (realgar);
<Calcination of gems>
gems other than <s>vajra</s> (diamond) are indeed calcined by eight <s>puṭas</s> (sealed heatings). // Rmañj_3.100 //
<s>Muktā</s> (pearl), <s>vidruma</s> (coral), <s>vajra</s> (diamond), <s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's eye), <s>sphaṭika</s> (crystal), and others — // Rmañj_3.101 //

children.text: maṇiratnaṃ kharaṃ śītaṃ kaṣāyaṃ svādu lekhanam /
children.translated_text: gem-stones are rough, cooling, astringent, sweet, and scraping;
they are beneficial for the eyes, and by wearing them, they remove sin, misfortune, and poison. // Rmañj_3.102 //
<The eighteen poisons>
The poison should be known as of eighteen kinds, declared to be tuber-born;

children.text: kālakūṭaṃ mayūrākhyaṃ bindukaṃ saktukaṃ tathā // Rmañj_4.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kālakūṭa</s>, <s>Mayūra</s> (peacock poison), <s>Binduka</s>, and <s>Saktuka</s> — // Rmañj_4.1 //
<s>Vāluka</s>, <s>Vatsanābha</s> (aconite), <s>Śaṅkhanābha</s>, and <s>Sumaṅgala</s>;

children.text: śṛṅgīṃ markaṭakaṃ mustaṃ kardamaṃ puṣkaraṃ śikhī // Rmañj_4.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Markaṭaka</s>, <s>Musta</s>, <s>Kardama</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, and <s>Śikhī</s> — // Rmañj_4.2 //
<s>Hāridra</s>, <s>Harita</s>, <s>Cakra</s>, and the poison called <s>Hālāhala</s>.
<Appearance of poisons>

children.text: ghanaṃ rūkṣaṃ ca kaṭhinaṃ bhinnāñjanasamaprabham // Rmañj_4.3 //
children.translated_text: Dense, rough, and hard, with lustre resembling split collyrium — // Rmañj_4.3 //
<s>Kālakūṭa</s>, the great poison, is described as tuber-shaped.

children.text: mayūrābhaṃ mayūrākhyaṃ binduvad bindukaḥ smṛtaḥ // Rmañj_4.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mayūra</s> (peacock poison) resembles a peacock; <s>Binduka</s> is known as drop-shaped. // Rmañj_4.4 //
Variegated, resembling a water-lily tuber — <s>Saktuka</s> is like parched grain;

children.text: vālukaṃ vālukākāraṃ vatsanābhaṃ tu pāṇḍuram // Rmañj_4.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vāluka</s> is sand-shaped, and <s>Vatsanābha</s> (aconite) is pale. // Rmañj_4.5 //
<s>Śaṅkhanābha</s> is conch-coloured, <s>Sumaṅgala</s> is of bright white colour;

children.text: ghanaṃ guruṃ ca niviḍaṃ śṛṅgākāraṃ tu śṛṅgikam // Rmañj_4.6 //
children.translated_text: dense, heavy, and compact — <s>Śṛṅgika</s> is horn-shaped. // Rmañj_4.6 //
<s>Markaṭa</s> is monkey-coloured, <s>Mustaka</s> resembles the <s>mustā</s> (nut-grass) root;

children.text: kardamaṃ kardamākāraṃ sitaṃ pītaṃ ca kardamam // Rmañj_4.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kardama</s> is mud-shaped — white, yellow, and mud-like. // Rmañj_4.7 //
<s>Puṣkara</s> resembles a lotus, <s>Śikhī</s> has the lustre of a peacock's crest;

children.text: hāridrakaṃ haridrābhaṃ haritaṃ haritaṃ smṛtam // Rmañj_4.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hāridraka</s> resembles turmeric, and <s>Harita</s> is known as green. // Rmañj_4.8 //
<s>Cakra</s> is disc-shaped, and <s>Halāhala</s> is blue-coloured.
Among these, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (priestly) variety is pale, the <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior) variety is red-coloured; // Rmañj_4.9 //

children.text: vaiśyaḥ pītaprabhaḥ śūdraḥ kṛṣṇābho ninditaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>vaiśya</s> (merchant) variety has a yellow hue; the <s>śūdra</s> (servant) variety is dark-coloured and is considered inferior.
The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> variety is given in diseases, the <s>kṣatriya</s> for poison-consumption;

children.text: vaiśyo vyādhiṣu sarveṣu sarpadaṣṭāya śūdrakam // Rmañj_4.10 //
children.translated_text: the <s>vaiśya</s> in all ailments, and the <s>śūdra</s> variety for snakebite. // Rmañj_4.10 //
<Killing of poison (calcination)>
That poison ground with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) is said to be killed (calcined);

children.text: yojayet sarvarogeṣu na vikāraṃ karoti hi // Rmañj_4.11 //
children.translated_text: it should be employed in all diseases — it does not cause any adverse effect. // Rmañj_4.11 //
<Purification of poison>

children.text: viṣabhāgāṃśca kaṇavat sthūlān kṛtvā tu bhājane /
children.translated_text: Having made the poison portions into coarse grain-sized pieces in a vessel,

children.text: tataḥ gomūtrakaṃ kṣiptvā pratyahaṃ nityanūtanam // Rmañj_4.12 //
children.translated_text: then adding cow's urine, fresh each day, // Rmañj_4.12 //
one should dry it after three days, then placing it in intense sunlight;
one should employ that poison in preparations according to the prescribed measure. // Rmañj_4.13 //

children.text: viṣasya māraṇaṃ proktamatha sevāṃ pravacmyaham // Rmañj_4.14 //
children.translated_text: The calcination of poison has been described; now I shall explain its administration. // Rmañj_4.14 //
In autumn, summer, spring, and in the rains one should administer it;
during the four-month period it removes diseases including <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases) and <s>lūtā</s> (spider-venom). // Rmañj_4.15 //
On the first day, the dose is one mustard seed; on the second, two mustard seeds;

children.text: tṛtīye ca caturthe ca pañcame divase tathā // Rmañj_4.16 //
children.translated_text: on the third, fourth, and fifth days likewise — // Rmañj_4.16 //

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe ca saptame caiva kramavṛddhyā vivardhayet /
children.translated_text: on the sixth and seventh, one should increase progressively;
the first week completes with a dose of seven mustard seeds. // Rmañj_4.17 //

children.text: kramahāniṃ tathā pakṣe dvitīyaṃ saptakaṃ viṣam /
children.translated_text: In the second week, the poison is given with progressive decrease;

children.text: yavamātraṃ viṣaṃ deyaṃ tṛtīye saptake kramāt // Rmañj_4.18 //
children.translated_text: in the third week, a barley-grain measure of poison should be given progressively. // Rmañj_4.18 //

children.text: vṛddhyāṃ hānyāṃ ca dātavyaṃ caturthasaptake tathā /
children.translated_text: In the fourth week, it should be given both with increase and decrease;

children.text: yavamātraṃ graset svastho guñjāmātraṃ tu kuṣṭhavān // Rmañj_4.19 //
children.translated_text: a healthy person should take a barley-grain measure, while a person with <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease) should take a <s>guñjā</s>-seed measure. // Rmañj_4.19 //
One whose age is eighty years or eight years —

children.text: viṣaṃ tasmai na dātavyaṃ dattaṃ ced doṣakārakam // Rmañj_4.20 //
children.translated_text: poison should not be given to such a person; if given, it causes harm. // Rmañj_4.20 //
One should give it in all diseases to one who eats wholesome food and follows a proper diet;
a milk-based diet should be employed for a person devoted to <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy). // Rmañj_4.21 //
<s>Brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) is of primary importance; one should observe it during the poison regimen;

children.text: pathye svasthamanā bhūtvātadā siddhirna saṃśayaḥ // Rmañj_4.22 //
children.translated_text: being of steady mind and following the prescribed diet, success is then certain, there is no doubt. // Rmañj_4.22 //
When a mortal inadvertently consumes poison in excess of the proper dose,

children.text: aṣṭau vegāstadā tasya jāyante nātra saṃśayaḥ // Rmañj_4.23 //
children.translated_text: then eight stages of reaction arise in him — there is no doubt about this. // Rmañj_4.23 //
In the first stage, anxiety; in the second, trembling occurs;

children.text: tṛtīye ghoradāhaḥ syāccaturthe patanaṃ bhuvi // Rmañj_4.24 //
children.translated_text: in the third, there is terrible burning; in the fourth, falling to the ground. // Rmañj_4.24 //

children.text: phenaṃ tu pañcame vege ṣaṣṭhe vikalatā bhavet /
children.translated_text: In the fifth stage, frothing; in the sixth, paralysis occurs;

children.text: jaḍatā saptame vege maraṇaṃ cāṣṭame bhavet // Rmañj_4.25 //
children.translated_text: in the seventh stage, stupor; and in the eighth, death occurs. // Rmañj_4.25 //
Having recognized the stages of poisoning, one should counteract them through <s>mantras</s> (incantations) and <s>tantras</s> (procedures);
for the benefit of practitioners, as uttered from the mouth of <s>Sadāśiva</s> —

body.translated_text: this supreme <s>mantra</s> is proclaimed for the destruction of all poisons. // Rmañj_4.27 //

body.text: oṃ namo bhagavate ghoṇeyan hara hara dara dara para para tara tara bara bara vadha vadha vaḥ vaḥ laḥ laḥ raṃ raṃ lāṃ lāṃ lāṃ haralāṃ hara hara bhava sara rāṃ rāṃ kṣīṃ kṣīṃ hīṃ hīṃ bhagavati śrīghoṇeyan saṃ saṃ saṃ vara vara rasaḥ dha vara vara khaṇḍa ca rūpa hrīṃ vara vihaṃgama mānuṣa yogakṣemaṃ vada śeṣāre śeṣāre ṣaṣaḥ svāhā // Rmañj_4.28 //
body.translated_text: Oṃ namo bhagavate ghoṇeyan hara hara dara dara para para tara tara bara bara vadha vadha vaḥ vaḥ laḥ laḥ raṃ raṃ lāṃ lāṃ lāṃ haralāṃ hara hara bhava sara rāṃ rāṃ kṣīṃ kṣīṃ hīṃ hīṃ bhagavati śrīghoṇeyan saṃ saṃ saṃ vara vara rasaḥ dha vara vara khaṇḍa ca rūpa hrīṃ vara vihaṃgama mānuṣa yogakṣemaṃ vada śeṣāre śeṣāre ṣaṣaḥ svāhā // Rmañj_4.28 //

children.translated_text: This <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) — merely by remembering it, <s>gutthaka</s> and other poisons are destroyed;

children.text: sapta japtena toyena prokṣayet kālacoditam // Rmañj_4.29 //
children.translated_text: by sprinkling with water over which it has been recited seven times, one who has been afflicted by fate — // Rmañj_4.29 //
rises up with vigour; one should wear it bound at the crown of the head;

children.text: trimantritena śaṃkhena dundubhir vādayed yadi // Rmañj_4.30 //
children.translated_text: if a drum made from a thrice-consecrated conch is sounded — // Rmañj_4.30 //
it renders the poison harmless instantly, even in another region or in the body.
When the <s>mantra</s>-adept sees poison and recites the <s>mantra</s> even once,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā nirviṣatāṃ yāti api māraśatāni ca // Rmañj_4.31 //
children.translated_text: upon seeing it, even hundreds of deadly poisons become harmless. // Rmañj_4.31 //
By drinking cow's ghee one overcomes various poisons; and <s>vandhyakarkoṭī</s> (a plant),
<s>triśūlikā</s> (a plant), and <s>surabhijihvā</s> (a plant) — these pacify the ill effects of all poisons. // Rmañj_4.32 //
<Calcination of poison>
Poison is calcined by grinding with <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulphate) and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax);

children.text: atimātraṃ tadā bhuṅkte tadājyaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ pibet // Rmañj_4.33 //
children.translated_text: when one has consumed an excessive amount, one should then drink ghee with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax). // Rmañj_4.33 //

children.text: na dātavyaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ viṣaṃ vāde kadācana /
children.translated_text: Poison should never be given or consumed in disputes;
the teacher alone should consume it, for the purpose of generating faith in the disciple. // Rmañj_4.34 //
Rmañj, 5
I shall describe the purification, calcination, properties, and reliable preparations from gold to the end of metal dross,
as spoken from the mouth of the <s>guru</s> (teacher). // Rmañj_5.1 //
<Metals: purification>

children.text: taile takre gavāṃ mūtre kvāthe kaulatthakāñjike /
children.translated_text: In oil, buttermilk, cow's urine, decoction of <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram), and <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel),

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ niṣecettu tattaddrāve tu saptadhā // Rmañj_5.2 //
children.translated_text: having heated and heated again, one should quench it seven times in each of those liquids. // Rmañj_5.2 //
From gold to the end of all metals, purification is certainly achieved;

children.text: śodhanaṃ māraṇaṃ caiva kathyate ca mayādhunā // Rmañj_5.3 //
children.translated_text: the purification and calcination are now described by me. // Rmañj_5.3 //
<Gold: purification>
Clay moistened with <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) juice for five days,
one should purify gold with <s>bhasma</s> (ash) and <s>lavaṇa</s> (salt) through <s>puṭapāka</s> (sealed heating). // Rmañj_5.4 //
<Gold bhasma (ash)>
Gold in equal measure with purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should be made into a ball in a mortar;

children.text: adhordhvaṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā sarvaṃ tulyaṃ nirudhya ca // Rmañj_5.5 //
children.translated_text: placing <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) above and below, all in equal proportion, sealing it — // Rmañj_5.5 //
thirty cowdung-cakes should be used for firing; thus fourteen <s>puṭas</s> (sealed heatings);

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma gandho deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ // Rmañj_5.6 //
children.translated_text: a non-revivable <s>bhasma</s> (ash) is produced; <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) should be added again and again. // Rmañj_5.6 //
<Gold bhasma>
Having made gold leaves pierceable by a thorn, one should coat them
with citron-water, <s>bhasma</s> (ash), and <s>sūta</s> (mercury) — it is calcined in ten <s>puṭas</s> (sealed heatings). // Rmañj_5.7 //
<Gold bhasma>
With the <s>bhasma</s> (ash) of mercury or with mercury itself, one should coat the foil;
one should coat it equally with <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), <s>sindūra</s> (red lead), and <s>śilā</s> (orpiment). // Rmañj_5.8 //
Grinding with gold-dissolving liquids for a day, then making it into a ball,

children.text: taṃ bhāṇḍasya tale dhṛtvā bhasmanā pūrayeddṛḍham // Rmañj_5.9 //
children.translated_text: placing it at the bottom of a vessel, one should fill it firmly with <s>bhasma</s> (ash). // Rmañj_5.9 //
One should kindle a strong fire for two nights; let it cool on its own;

children.text: uddhṛtya sāvaśeṣaṃ ca punardeyaṃ puṭatrayam // Rmañj_5.10 //
children.translated_text: extracting it, if any residue remains, three more <s>puṭas</s> (sealed heatings) should be given. // Rmañj_5.10 //
By this method, gold becomes non-revivable and boundless in potency;

children.text: etadrasāyanaṃ balyaṃ vṛṣyaṃ śītaṃ kṣayādihṛt // Rmañj_5.11 //
children.translated_text: this is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative), strengthening, aphrodisiac, cooling, and destroys <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption) and other diseases. // Rmañj_5.11 //
<Gold bhasma>
To melted gold, one-sixteenth part of <s>sīsaka</s> (lead) should be added;
having combined and extracted it, one should grind it with lemon juice. // Rmañj_5.12 //
Equal to that ball, <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) powder should be placed above and below;
placing it in a sealed pair of saucers, one should fire it with twenty cowdung-cakes. // Rmañj_5.13 //
Thus with sage-measured <s>puṭas</s>, gold does not regain its original form.
<Gold bhasma>

children.text: mākṣikaṃ nāgacūrṇaṃ ca piṣṭamarkarase punaḥ // Rmañj_5.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite) and <s>nāga</s> (lead) powder, ground again in the juice of <s>arka</s> (calotropis) — // Rmañj_5.14 //
gold foil treated with this is calcined in an instant.
<Gold: medicinal properties>
Gold is astringent, bitter, and sweet; it is heavy and scraping; // Rmañj_5.15 //

children.text: vṛṣyaṃ rasāyanaṃ balyaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ kāntidaṃ śuci /
children.translated_text: it is aphrodisiac, rejuvenative, strengthening, beneficial for the eyes, lustre-giving, and pure;
it bestows longevity, lustre, stability of age, purity of speech, and memory. // Rmañj_5.16 //
It is declared to be the supreme pacifier for those afflicted with <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption), <s>unmāda</s> (insanity), and other diseases.
<Purification of silver>
One desiring purification should melt it with one part of <s>kṣārarāja</s> (alkaline salt). // Rmañj_5.17 //
<Silver bhasma (ash)>
Four parts of silver foil and one part of purified <s>tālaka</s> (realgar);
one should grind and coat the silver foils with <s>jambīra</s> (lemon) juices. // Rmañj_5.18 //
Sealed and fired with three <s>puṭas</s> using twenty-five cowdung-cakes;

children.text: mriyate nātra sandeho gandho deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ // Rmañj_5.19 //
children.translated_text: it is calcined without doubt — <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) should be added again and again. // Rmañj_5.19 //
<Silver bhasma>
Equal parts of <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold pyrite) and <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) should be prepared;

children.text: arkakṣīreṇa sampiṣṭaṃ tārapatraṃ pralipya ca // Rmañj_5.20 //
children.translated_text: ground with the milky sap of <s>arka</s> (calotropis), one should coat the silver foil. // Rmañj_5.20 //
Firing silver by <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating), it certainly becomes calcined.
<Silver: calcination (method 3)>

children.text: vidhāya piṣṭiṃ sūtena rajatasyātha melayet // Rmañj_5.21 //
children.translated_text: Having prepared an amalgam with mercury, one should combine it with silver; // Rmañj_5.21 //
then <s>tāla</s> (realgar) and <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) in equal parts should be ground with lemon juice;

children.text: dvitraiḥ puṭaiḥ bhavedbhasma yojyameva rasādiṣu // Rmañj_5.22 //
children.translated_text: with two or three <s>puṭas</s> (sealed heatings), <s>bhasma</s> (ash) is produced, suitable for use in mercurial and other preparations. // Rmañj_5.22 //
<Silver: medicinal properties>
It is cooling, astringent, sweet, and sour; it overcomes disorders caused by <s>vāta</s> (wind);
it is appetite-stimulating, strength-giving, unctuous, and destroys severe indigestion;

children.text: āyuṣyaṃ dīrgharogaghnaṃ rajataṃ lekhanaṃ param // Rmañj_5.23 //
children.translated_text: silver is life-prolonging, cures chronic diseases, and is supremely scraping. // Rmañj_5.23 //
<Copper>
They say poison is not truly poison — it is copper that is called poison.
<Copper: eight defects>

children.text: eko doṣo viṣe tāmre tvaṣṭau doṣāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // Rmañj_5.24 //
children.translated_text: Poison has one defect, but copper is declared to have eight defects. // Rmañj_5.24 //
<s>Bhrama</s> (dizziness), <s>mūrcchā</s> (fainting), <s>vidāha</s> (burning sensation), <s>sveda</s> (sweating), <s>kledana</s> (moistening), and <s>vānti</s> (vomiting);
<s>aruci</s> (loss of appetite) and <s>cittasantāpa</s> (mental distress) — these defects are comparable to poison. // Rmañj_5.25 //
Therefore, only well-purified copper should be used for the alleviation of diseases.
<Copper: purification>
One should coat the copper foil with salts and <s>vajra</s> (euphorbia) milk; // Rmañj_5.26 //

children.text: agnau saṃtāpya nirguṇḍīrasaiḥ siktaṃ ca saptadhā /
children.translated_text: heating it in fire and quenching it seven times in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (vitex) juice;
similarly in the sap of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (calotropis) — the purification of copper will be achieved. // Rmañj_5.27 //
<Copper: purification>
One should boil a copper foil in cow's urine for three hours over a strong fire;

children.text: śudhyate nātra sandeho māraṇaṃ vāpyathocyate // Rmañj_5.28 //
children.translated_text: it is purified — there is no doubt; now <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination) is also described. // Rmañj_5.28 //
<s>Tāmra Bhasma</s> (Calcined Copper Ash)

children.text: sūtamekaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ yāmaṃ kanyāṃ vimardayet /
children.translated_text: One part mercury, two parts sulphur — one should grind with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe vera juice) for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours);

children.text: dvayostulyaṃ tāmrapatraṃ sthālyā garbhaṃ nirodhayet // Rmañj_5.29 //
children.translated_text: an equal amount of copper foil [to the two combined] should be sealed inside a crucible. // Rmañj_5.29 //

children.text: samyaṅ mṛllavaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ pārśve bhasma nidhāya ca /
children.translated_text: Properly sealed with clay and salt, placing ash on the sides,
one should heat on a stove for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours), with cow dung on the back of the vessel. // Rmañj_5.30 //
Water should be added again and again; when cooled to body temperature, one should powder it.

children.text: mriyate nātra sandehaḥ sarvayogeṣu yojayet // Rmañj_5.31 //
children.translated_text: It dies [i.e., is calcined] — there is no doubt; it should be employed in all preparations. // Rmañj_5.31 //
<s>Tāmra Bhasma</s> (Calcined Copper Ash, method 2)
One should coat copper foils with mercury in one-fourth proportion;
ground with sour substances, doubled in quantity, one should apply the offering above and below. // Rmañj_5.32 //
In a vessel filled with the paste of <s>cāṅgerī</s> (Oxalis corniculata), one should heat firmly for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours).
The copper foil becomes <s>bhasma</s> (ash) — it should be employed in all preparations. // Rmañj_5.33 //
<s>Tāmra Bhasma</s> (Calcined Copper Ash, method 3)
Ground with lemon juice, coated with mercury and sulphur,
the copper foil, placed in a saucer-seal, attains death [i.e., is calcined] by three <s>tripuṭa</s> heatings. // Rmañj_5.34 //

children.text: tāmraṃ tiktāmlamadhuraṃ kaṣāyaṃ śītalaṃ param // Rmañj_5.35 //
