children.translated_text: Copper is bitter, sour, sweet, astringent, and supremely cooling. // Rmañj_5.35 //
It destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and wasting diseases; it destroys skin diseases affecting the bodily tissues, and is a rejuvenative;
it destroys colic and hemorrhoids, as <s>Indra's</s> thunderbolt [destroys] a tree. // Rmañj_5.36 //
Purification and Calcination of <s>Rājarīti</s> (Brass) and <s>Ghoṣa</s> (Bell-metal)
<s>Rājarīti</s> (brass) and <s>ghoṣa</s> (bell-metal) should be calcined separately like copper;
their purification is like that of copper, and their properties are similar to copper. // Rmañj_5.37 //
Purification of <s>Nāga</s> (Lead) and <s>Vaṅga</s> (Tin)
<s>Nāga</s> (lead) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), when melted, should be quenched with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk;
done three times, they attain purity, [poured through] a perforated pot. // Rmañj_5.38 //
Calcination of Lead (method 1)
<s>Nāga</s> (lead) ground with the juice of <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda vasica) [is calcined] with three <s>kumbhapuṭas</s> (pot-heatings);

children.text: sā śilā bhasmatāmeti tadrajaḥ sarvamehahṛt // Rmañj_5.39 //
children.translated_text: that mineral attains the state of ash — its powder destroys all urinary diseases. // Rmañj_5.39 //
<s>Nāga Bhasma</s> (Calcined Lead Ash, method 2)

children.text: bhūbhujaṅgam agastiṃ ca piṣṭvā pātraṃ vilepayet /
children.translated_text: One should grind <s>bhūbhujaṅga</s> (earthworm) and <s>Agasti</s> (Sesbania grandiflora) and coat the vessel with it;
into molten lead, [add] the juice derived from <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda) and <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera). // Rmañj_5.40 //
One should mix in alkali to one-fourth proportion, as stated by the preceptor;

children.text: praharaṃ pācayeccullyāṃ vāsādarvyā ca ghaṭṭitā // Rmañj_5.41 //
children.translated_text: one should heat on a stove for one <s>prahara</s> (three hours), stirring with a <s>vāsā</s>-wood ladle. // Rmañj_5.41 //
Then, having extracted that powder, one should grind it with <s>vāsā</s> juice;

children.text: puṭet punaḥ samuddhṛtya tenaiva parimardayet // Rmañj_5.42 //
children.translated_text: one should give a <s>puṭa</s> (heating) again, extract it, and grind it with the same [juice]. // Rmañj_5.42 //

children.text: evaṃ sapta puṭaṃ nāgaṃ sindūraṃ jāyate dhruvam /
children.translated_text: Thus, with seven <s>puṭas</s> (heatings), lead assuredly becomes a vermillion-like [ash].
Qualities of <s>Nāga Bhasma</s> (Calcined Lead Ash)
<s>Nāga</s> (lead), which stands [allied with] silver, is a coloring agent and removes <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm). // Rmañj_5.43 //
It removes <s>grahaṇī</s> (sprue), skin diseases, urinary disorders, hemorrhoids, wasting of vital breath, and poisons.
Calcination of Tin (method 1)
<s>Ābhīra</s> [i.e., tin] should first be purified, then melted in a pot. // Rmañj_5.44 //
Then, powdered <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera) in one-fourth proportion should be added;
one should stir it slowly with a thick-tipped iron ladle. // Rmañj_5.45 //
Until it attains the state of ash, it should be ground as before;
then the whole, unified, becomes charcoal-colored. // Rmañj_5.46 //
The physician should seal it inside with a fresh earthen saucer;
thereafter, heated with intense fire, it assuredly becomes <s>vaṅga bhasma</s> (tin ash). // Rmañj_5.47 //
Calcination of Tin (method 2)

children.text: vaṅgaṃ satālamarkasya piṣṭvā dugdhena taṃ puṭet /
children.translated_text: Tin ground with <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) should be given a <s>puṭa</s> (heating) with milk;
with dried barks of <s>aśvattha</s> (Ficus religiosa), it reaches the state of ash in seven [puṭas]. // Rmañj_5.48 //
Qualities of <s>Vaṅga Bhasma</s> (Calcined Tin Ash)
<s>Vaṅga</s> (tin) is bitter, hot, and dry, slightly aggravating <s>vāta</s> (wind);
it destroys urinary diseases and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) disorders, and destroys worms and delusion. // Rmañj_5.49 //
Purification of Iron (of mountain origin)
In water eight times the quantity of <s>triphalā</s>, sixteen <s>palas</s> of <s>triphalā</s> [are taken];

children.text: tatkvāthe pādaśeṣe tu lohasya palapañcakam // Rmañj_5.50 //
children.translated_text: in that decoction reduced to one-fourth, five <s>palas</s> of iron [are placed]. // Rmañj_5.50 //
Having made foils, the heated [foils] should be quenched seven times;

children.text: evaṃ pralīyate doṣo girijo lohasambhavaḥ // Rmañj_5.51 //
children.translated_text: thus the defect born of iron's mountain origin dissolves. // Rmañj_5.51 //
<s>Loha Bhasma</s> (Calcined Iron Ash, method 1)
One part of purified mercury, two parts of <s>bala</s> (Sida cordifolia) [juice],

children.text: dvayoḥ samaṃ sāracūrṇaṃ mardayet kanyakāmbunā // Rmañj_5.52 //
children.translated_text: and an equal amount of iron powder to the two [combined] — one should grind with <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe) water. // Rmañj_5.52 //
For two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours), then the ball should be placed in a copper vessel;
covered with castor leaves, it should remain warm for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours). // Rmañj_5.53 //

children.text: tridinaṃ dhānyarāśisthaṃ taṃ tato mardayed dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Kept in a heap of grain for three days, it should then be ground firmly;
that powder, filtered through cloth, floats on water like a swan. // Rmañj_5.54 //

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ muṇḍaṃ kāntalohaṃ nirutthaṃ jāyate mṛtam /
children.translated_text: <s>Tīkṣṇa</s> (steel), <s>muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron), and <s>kāntaloha</s> (magnetic iron) — [each] becomes dead [i.e., calcined] without rising;
combined with <s>triphalā</s> and honey, this should be consumed as a rejuvenative. // Rmañj_5.55 //
<s>Loha Bhasma</s> (Calcined Iron Ash, method 2)
One should mix <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) in one-twelfth proportion with iron powder;
grinding with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) juice for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours), one should give a <s>puṭa</s> (heating);

children.text: puṭedevaṃ lohacūrṇaṃ saptadhā maraṇaṃ vrajet // Rmañj_5.56 //
children.translated_text: thus given <s>puṭa</s> heatings, the iron powder reaches calcination in seven [cycles]. // Rmañj_5.56 //
<s>Loha Bhasma</s> (Calcined Iron Ash, method 3)
One should quench iron foils in the juice of <s>kākodumbarikā</s> (Ficus hispida);
heated repeatedly, they should be pounded six times in a mortar. // Rmañj_5.57 //
Adding <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) in one-fifth proportion, one should grind the whole;

children.text: kumārīnīratas tīkṣṇaṃ puṭe gajapuṭe tathā // Rmañj_5.58 //
children.translated_text: with <s>kumārī</s> (aloe) juice, the steel should be given a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-sized heating). // Rmañj_5.58 //
Three times with <s>triphalā</s> decoctions, the same number of times, diligently;
thus with fourteen <s>puṭas</s> (heatings), iron becomes <s>vāritara</s> (floating on water). // Rmañj_5.59 //
<s>Loha Bhasma</s> (Calcined Iron Ash, method 4)
Coating a sword with the pulp of <s>tindūphala</s> (Diospyros embryopteris) fruit, [keeping it] in harsh sunlight,
one should hold it with a bronze vessel — in one day it is sufficiently calcined. // Rmañj_5.60 //

children.text: lepaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kuryād dinānte tatprapeṣayet /
children.translated_text: One should apply the coating again and again; at the end of the day, one should grind it;
combined with <s>triphalā</s> decoction, death [i.e., calcination] occurs in one day. // Rmañj_5.61 //
<s>Loha Bhasma</s> (Calcined Iron Ash, method 5)

children.text: lohaṃ patramatīva taptamasakṛtkvāthe kṣipettraiphale cūrṇībhūtamato bhavet triphalaje kvāthe pacet gojale /
children.translated_text: Iron foil, heated intensely, should be cast repeatedly into <s>triphalā</s> decoction; having become powder, it should be cooked in <s>triphalā</s> decoction and cow's urine;

children.text: matsyākṣītriphalārasena puṭayedyāvannirutthaṃ bhavet paścādājyamadhuplutaṃ supuṭitaṃ bhasma bhaved āyasam // Rmañj_5.62 //
children.translated_text: one should give <s>puṭas</s> with the juice of <s>matsyākṣī</s> (Alternanthera sessilis) and <s>triphalā</s> until it becomes <s>niruttha</s> (non-rising); thereafter, immersed in ghee and honey and well-calcined, it becomes iron ash. // Rmañj_5.62 //
Checking the <s>Vāritara</s> (Water-floating) State of Iron
All this calcined iron should be blown [with bellows] upon the five dead [metals];

children.text: yadyeva syānnirutthānaṃ satyaṃ vāritaraṃ bhavet // Rmañj_5.63 //
children.translated_text: if indeed it is non-rising, then it is truly <s>vāritara</s> (water-floating). // Rmañj_5.63 //
<s>Loha Niruttha Bhasma</s> (Non-rising Iron Ash)

children.text: gandhakaṃ tutthakaṃ lohaṃ tulyaṃ khalve vimardayet /
children.translated_text: Sulphur, <s>tutthaka</s> (blue vitriol), and iron in equal parts should be ground in a mortar;
for one day with <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe) liquids, sealed and heated in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-sized heating);
thus, for all irons, the non-rising state should be achieved in this manner. // Rmañj_5.64 //
Qualities of <s>Loha Bhasma</s> (Calcined Iron Ash)
Black iron destroys colic, hemorrhoids, skin diseases, anemia, and urinary disorders;

children.text: vayaḥsthaṃ guru cakṣuṣyaṃ saraṃ medogadāpaham // Rmañj_5.65 //
children.translated_text: it maintains youthfulness, is heavy, good for the eyes, laxative, and removes diseases of fat. // Rmañj_5.65 //

children.text: āyuḥpradātā balavīryakartā rogasya hartā madanasya kartā /
children.translated_text: It is a giver of longevity, a maker of strength and virility, a remover of disease, and a creator of desire;

children.text: ayaḥsamānaṃ nahi kiṃcid anyad rasāyanaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ hi janto // Rmañj_5.66 //
children.translated_text: nothing else equals iron — it is the most excellent rejuvenative, O being! // Rmañj_5.66 //

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ tilatailaṃ ca māṣānnaṃ rājakaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd), sesame oil, <s>māṣa</s> (black gram) food, and alkali —
liquor, sour substances — these should be avoided by one who consumes iron [preparations]. // Rmañj_5.67 //
<s>Muṇḍa</s> (Wrought Iron / Iron Slag)

children.text: ye guṇā mārite muṇḍe te guṇā muṇḍakiṭṭake /
children.translated_text: The properties that are in calcined <s>muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron), those same properties are in <s>muṇḍakiṭṭa</s> (iron slag);

children.text: tasmāt sarvatra maṇḍūraṃ rogaśāntyai niyojayet // Rmañj_5.68 //
children.translated_text: therefore, one should employ <s>maṇḍūra</s> (iron rust/slag) everywhere for the pacification of diseases. // Rmañj_5.68 //
Slag of hundred years is the best, of eighty years is middling,

children.text: adhamaṃ ṣaṣṭivarṣīyaṃ tato hīnaṃ viṣopamam // Rmañj_5.69 //
children.translated_text: of sixty years is inferior, and less than that is like poison. // Rmañj_5.69 //
The impurity of iron, burnt with <s>akṣa</s> (Terminalia bellirica) wood and quenched eight times with cow's urine,

children.text: vicūrṇya līḍhaṃ madhunācireṇa nṛṇāṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍugadaṃ nihanti // Rmañj_5.70 //
children.translated_text: powdered and licked with honey, quickly destroys wasting and anemia in people. // Rmañj_5.70 //
<s>Muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron) is ten times [more potent] than slag; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (steel) is a hundred times more than <s>muṇḍa</s>;

children.text: tīkṣṇāllakṣaguṇaṃ kāntaṃ bhakṣaṇāt kurute guṇam // Rmañj_5.71 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> (magnetic iron) is a hundred-thousand times more than steel — it produces benefit when consumed. // Rmañj_5.71 //
<s>Rasamañjarī</s>, Chapter 6
The god who arose from the ocean of milk, wearing yellow garments, four-armed —
I salute <s>Dhanvantari</s> always, the destroyer of manifold diseases. // Rmañj_6.1 //

children.text: yathā gurumukhaṃ śrutvā sānubhūtaṃ ca tadrasam /
children.translated_text: Having heard from the teacher's mouth and having experienced its essence,

children.text: sa rasaḥ procyate hyatra vyādhināśanahetave // Rmañj_6.2 //
children.translated_text: that <s>rasa</s> (mercurial medicine) is proclaimed here for the purpose of destroying diseases. // Rmañj_6.2 //
Except for one who is a <s>rasavaidya</s> (mercurial physician), [endowed with] gain, honor, and fame,

children.text: tṛṇakāṣṭhauṣadhair vaidyaḥ ko labheta varāṭikām // Rmañj_6.3 //
children.translated_text: what physician using [mere] grass, wood, and herbs would obtain even a cowrie shell? // Rmañj_6.3 //

children.text: yasya rogasya yo yogo munibhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For whichever disease, whichever formulation has been proclaimed by the sages,
the physician should employ mercury combined with that very formulation. // Rmañj_6.4 //

children.text: mātrādhikaṃ na seveta rasaṃ vā viṣam auṣadham /
children.translated_text: One should not consume <s>rasa</s> (mercury), poison, or medicine in excessive dose;

children.text: tryādhibaddhaṃ ca koṣṭhaṃ ca vīkṣya mātrāṃ prayojayet // Rmañj_6.5 //
children.translated_text: having examined the three <s>adhis</s> (constitutions) and the bowel, one should administer the [proper] dose. // Rmañj_6.5 //
<s>Ratnagarbha Poṭalī</s> (Gem-filled Bolus)

children.text: rasaṃ vajraṃ hema tāraṃ nāgaṃ lohaṃ ca tāmrakam /
children.translated_text: Mercury, diamond, gold, silver, lead, iron, and copper —
calcined in equal parts, one should add pearl, pyrite, and coral. // Rmañj_6.6 //
And conch in exactly equal parts — one should grind for seven days with the juices of <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago zeylanica);
then, having powdered it, one should fill a cowrie shell with it. // Rmañj_6.7 //

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ravidugdhena piṣṭvā mūṣāṃ ca bandhayet /
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk, one should seal the crucible;

children.text: mṛdbhāṇḍe ca nirudhyātha samyaggajapuṭe pacet // Rmañj_6.8 //
children.translated_text: then, sealing it in an earthen vessel, one should properly heat it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-sized heating). // Rmañj_6.8 //
When cooled to body temperature, having extracted it, one should make it into fine powder;
taking all of it, one should give seven levigations with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo) [juice]. // Rmañj_6.9 //
Seven [levigations] with fresh ginger juice, twenty-one with <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago) juices;

children.text: dravairbhāvyaṃ tataḥ śoṣyaṃ deyaṃ guñjācatuṣṭayam // Rmañj_6.10 //
children.translated_text: the liquid should be levigated, then dried; the dose is four <s>guñjās</s> (about 500 mg). // Rmañj_6.10 //
It quickly destroys <s>kṣayaroga</s> (consumption), whether curable or incurable — there is no doubt;
it should be administered with <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), honey, ghee, and black pepper. // Rmañj_6.11 //
In the eight great diseases, in cough, fever, dyspnea, and diarrhea —
this <s>Ratnagarbha Poṭalī</s> (gem-filled bolus) should be employed with appropriate vehicles. // Rmañj_6.12 //
<s>Mṛgāṅka Rasa</s> (Moon Elixir)

children.text: syādrasena samaṃ hema mauktikaṃ dviguṇaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Gold should be equal to mercury; pearl should be twice [that amount];

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca samaṃ tena rasapādastu ṭaṃkaṇam // Rmañj_6.13 //
children.translated_text: sulphur should be equal to that [pearl]; and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) should be one-fourth of the mercury. // Rmañj_6.13 //
Having made all of it into a ball, one should dry it with <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel);
in a vessel filled with salt, one should heat for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours). // Rmañj_6.14 //
Known by the name <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> (Moon), it is the cutter of the king of diseases [i.e., consumption];
the physician should administer four <s>guñjās</s> (about 500 mg) of this with black pepper. // Rmañj_6.15 //
Or the wise one should administer it as a linctus with ten <s>pippalīs</s> (long peppers) and honey;
the diet should mostly be light meat preparations. // Rmañj_6.16 //

children.text: dadhyājyagavyaṃ takraṃ vā kṣīraṃ vājaṃ prayojayet /
children.translated_text: Curd, ghee, cow's [products], buttermilk, or milk from a goat should be administered;
with side dishes that are mildly cooked, not too alkaline, and free of <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida). // Rmañj_6.17 //
Seasoned with cardamom, lemon, and black pepper, [foods should be] non-burning;
one should avoid <s>vṛntāka</s> (eggplant), [sesame] oil, <s>bilva</s> (Aegle marmelos), and <s>kāravella</s> (bitter gourd). // Rmañj_6.18 //

children.text: striyaṃ parihared dūrāt kopaṃ cāpi parityajet /
children.translated_text: One should keep away from women and also abandon anger;
the creeper named <s>tumbarikā</s> — one <s>pala</s> of its root should be decocted. // Rmañj_6.19 //
Combined with the three pungents, it should be given to drink for the pacification of cough;

children.text: triśūlī yā samākhyātā tanmūlaṃ kvāthayed valam // Rmañj_6.20 //
children.translated_text: the [plant] known as <s>triśūlī</s> — one <s>pala</s> of its root should be decocted. // Rmañj_6.20 //
Combined with a little <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), a <s>kākiṇī</s> [dose of] <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago) and <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag) —
one should consume it with wholesome food for the pacification of all diseases. // Rmañj_6.21 //
A pill made with honey from the powder of <s>markaṭī</s> (a plant) leaves
should be kept constantly in the mouth — it destroys cough and flatulence. // Rmañj_6.22 //
Goat meat, goat's milk, goat's ghee with <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger),
use of goat [products] along with endurance — [this regimen] among goat [products] destroys consumption. // Rmañj_6.23 //

children.text: malāyattaṃ balaṃ puṃsāṃ śukrāyattaṃ ca jīvitam /
children.translated_text: The strength of a person depends on [proper] waste [elimination]; life depends on <s>śukra</s> (reproductive fluid);
therefore, one should especially protect the waste and reproductive fluid of a consumptive patient. // Rmañj_6.24 //
<s>Lokanātha Rasa</s> (Lord of the World Elixir)
One <s>pala</s> of powdered cowrie shell, one <s>pala</s> each of mercury and sulphur —
One <s>māṣa</s> (unit) of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) also should be ground with lemon juice.
This <s>puṭa</s>-preparation is called <s>Lokeśvara</s> — this <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World) is excellent;
it conquers leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), other diseases, and removes consumption.
It is a bestower of nourishment and virility, and a supreme giver of beauty and charm;

children.text: ko'sti lokeśvarād anyo nṛṇāṃ śambhumukhodgatāt // Rmañj_6.27 //
children.translated_text: who else is there besides <s>Lokeśvara</s>, which has come from the mouth of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), for mankind?
<s>Lokeśvara Paṭolī Rasa</s>
One should prepare gold with a quarter-part of mercury ash;
having added double the quantity of sulphur, one should grind with the juice of <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago zeylanica).
Having filled cowry shells [with it] and sealed with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),

children.text: bhāṇḍe cūrṇaṃ pratilikhetkṣiptvā rundhīta mṛnmaye // Rmañj_6.29 //
children.translated_text: one should inscribe the powder on a vessel and place it, sealed, in an earthen pot.
Having dried it, one should calcine it in a <s>garbha</s>-furnace, adding fire in the afternoon;
having taken it out when cooled naturally, one should powder it and then apply.
This [preparation] called <s>Lokeśvara</s> is an increaser of virility and nourishment;
four <s>guñjā</s> doses of this, combined with <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) and honey,
should be eaten with supreme devotion — <s>Lokeśa</s> bestows all accomplishments.
In bodily emaciation, weak digestive fire, cough, and <s>pitta</s> (bile) disorders, this preparation
should be given with pepper combined with ghee, for three days;
salt should be avoided during that time; one should lie on one's back with feet raised.
For twenty-one days, one should drink pepper with ghee;
the diet should be given like [the regimen of] <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> [preparation]; one should lie on one's back with feet raised.

children.text: ye śuṣkā viṣamānilaiḥ kṣayarujā vyāptāśca ye kuṣṭhino ye pāṇḍutvahatāḥ kuvaidyavidhinā ye śoṣiṇo durbhagāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are dried out, afflicted with irregular <s>vāta</s> (wind) and consumptive diseases, those who are lepers, those who are struck by pallor, those emaciated and unfortunate due to quack remedies,

children.text: ye taptā vividhair jvarair bhramamadonmādaiḥ pramādaṃ gatāste sarve vigatāmayā hatarujaḥ syuḥ poṭalīsevayā // Rmañj_6.35 //
children.translated_text: those tormented by various fevers, vertigo, intoxication, and madness — all of them become disease-free and pain-free through the use of <s>poṭalī</s> (the preparation).
<s>Rājamṛgāṅka Rasa</s> (Royal Moon-marked Preparation)
Three parts of mercury ash, one part of gold ash,
one part of killed copper, and <s>śilā</s> (realgar), sulphur, and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) —
two parts each, purified — one should combine and powder them all together.
Having filled cowry shells with that, and [grinding] <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> with goat's milk,

children.text: piṣṭvā tena mukhaṃ ruddhvā mṛdbhāṇḍe ca nirodhayet /
children.translated_text: having sealed the mouth with that paste, one should seal it in an earthen vessel.
When dry, it should be cooked in an elephant-<s>puṭa</s> (large calcination); when cooled naturally, it should be powdered.
This preparation called <s>Rājamṛgāṅka</s>, in four-<s>guñjā</s> dose, removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);
with ten <s>pippalīs</s> (long peppers) and honey, and nineteen peppers
combined with ghee, it should be given as a decoction in consumption arising from <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm).
<s>Ratnagiri Rasa</s> (Mountain of Gems Preparation)

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ samaṃ gandhaṃ mṛtaṃ svarṇābhratāmrakam /
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, equal sulphur, killed gold, mica, and copper —
each equal to the mercury; half of the mercury as killed iron;
half of the iron as killed <s>vaikrānta</s> — one should grind with juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta alba).
It should be cooked like <s>parpaṭī</s>-preparation; when powdered, it should be treated separately
with [juices of] <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), <s>vāsaka</s> (Adhatoda), <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo), <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), <s>soma</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>;
<s>kṣudrā</s> (small), <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora), <s>jayantī</s>, <s>muni</s>, <s>brāhmī</s> (Bacopa), and <s>sutiktaka</s> (bitter herbs);
and with juices of <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) — treated with each juice three times, three times;

children.text: ruddhvā laghupuṭe pācyaṃ bhūdhare taṃ samuddharet // Rmañj_6.43 //
children.translated_text: having sealed it, it should be cooked in a light <s>puṭa</s>; one should extract it upon the ground.

body.text: imaṃ navajvare dadyānmāṣamātraṃ rasasya tu // Rmañj_6.44 //
body.translated_text: In new fever, one should give one <s>māṣa</s> measure of this preparation.

children.translated_text: Mixed with black cumin — within a <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes), the fever is gone.

children.text: ayaṃ ratnagirirnāma raso yogasya vāhakaḥ // Rmañj_6.45 //
children.translated_text: This [preparation] called <s>Ratnagiri</s> is a vehicle for the [medicinal] formulation.
<s>Hiṅguleśvara Rasa</s> (?)

children.text: tulyāṃśaṃ cūrṇayet khalve pippalīṃ hiṅgulaṃ viṣam /
children.translated_text: One should powder in a mortar equal parts of <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), and poison (<s>viṣa</s>, i.e., aconite);
two <s>guñjā</s> with honey should be given for the removal of <s>vāta</s>-fever.
<s>Śītabhañjī Rasa</s> (Cold-breaking Preparation)
Mercury, <s>rasaka</s> (zinc calamine), <s>tāla</s> (orpiment), <s>tuttha</s> (blue vitriol), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and sulphur —
all of these in equal parts, purified, with juices of <s>kāravellī</s> (bitter gourd) for one day —
one should grind, and with that paste, smear the inside of a copper vessel
to the thickness of half a finger, and cook in the apparatus called sand-bath,
until rice grains placed on its back burst open;
then the physician should collect it, well-cooled, from the inside of the copper vessel.
The [preparation] called <s>Śītabhañjī Rasa</s> should be powdered with equal pepper;
one <s>māṣa</s>, with a piece of betel leaf, should be eaten — it destroys fever,
irregular, severe, quotidian, tertian, and quartan [fevers] within three days.
<s>Śītabhañjī Rasa</s> [variant preparation]

children.text: rasahiṅgulagandhaṃ ca jaipālaṃ ca tribhiḥ samam /
children.translated_text: Mercury, cinnabar, and sulphur, and <s>jaipāla</s> (croton seed) — these three in equal parts,

children.text: dantīkvāthena saṃmardya raso jvaraharaḥ smṛtaḥ // Rmañj_6.51 //
children.translated_text: ground with the decoction of <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum) — this preparation is declared to be fever-destroying.
Then with the juice of fresh ginger, two <s>raktikā</s> doses should be given;
it destroys new fever, even of the most terrible kind, within one <s>yāma</s> (watch, 3 hours).

children.text: śarkarā dadhibhaktaṃ ca pathyaṃ deyaṃ prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: Sugar, yogurt-rice — this should be carefully given as the prescribed diet;
cold water should be drunk afterward; sugarcane juice is beneficial.
The [preparation] called <s>Śītabhañjī Rasa</s> is the destroyer of all fevers.
<s>Śītāri Rasa</s> (Enemy of Cold Preparation)

children.text: sūtakaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ gandhaṃ śulbacūrṇaṃ samaṃ samam /
children.translated_text: Mercury, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), sulphur, and copper powder — all in equal parts;
<s>jaipāla</s> (croton) seed without husk should be given in double the quantity of mercury.
<s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt), pepper, tamarind-bark ash, and sugar —

children.text: pratyekaṃ sūtatulyaṃ syājjambīrair mardayed dinam // Rmañj_6.55 //
children.translated_text: each equal to the mercury — one should grind with lemon [juice] for one day.
Two <s>guñjā</s> with hot water — it removes fever arising from <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm);
this preparation called <s>Śītāri</s> is the supreme destroyer of cold fevers.
One part of the king of mercury, and half a part of <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite);
two parts of <s>śilā</s> (realgar); three are prescribed for sulphur;
eighteen parts of <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment); five parts of copper;
three parts of <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut) — all should be powdered together.
Having drenched it with the milk of <s>vajrī</s> (Euphorbia), [place] in a sturdy earthen vessel.
Having made a firm seal, one should cook for four <s>yāmas</s> (watches);
having taken it out when cooled naturally, one should grind it firmly again.
Four <s>guñjā</s> of this should be given with a piece of betel leaf;
this well-known <s>Jvararāja</s> is the destroyer of eight types of fever.
In the morning after eating it, the prescribed diet is buttermilk-rice, which is beneficial;
combined with <s>tuttha</s> (blue vitriol) in [appropriate] proportion, it prevents quartan fever.
<s>Mahājvarāṅkuśa Rasa</s> (Great Fever-goad Preparation)

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ viṣaṃ tulyaṃ dhūrtabījaṃ tribhiḥ samam /
children.translated_text: Equal parts of mercury, sulphur, and poison (<s>viṣa</s>); <s>dhūrta</s>-seed (croton) equal to [those] three;
double the amount of that powder as <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) powder — two <s>guñjā</s> is the beneficial [dose].
Ground with the pulp of lemon and juices of fresh ginger —
this [preparation] called <s>Mahājvarāṅkuśa</s> (Great Fever-goad) is the cutter of eight types of fever.

children.text: aikāhikaṃ dvyāhikaṃ ca tryāhikaṃ ca caturthakam /
children.translated_text: Quotidian, tertian, every-two-days, quartan,

children.text: viṣamaṃ ca tridoṣotthaṃ hanti sarvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ // Rmañj_6.65 //
children.translated_text: irregular, and arising from the three <s>doṣas</s> — it destroys all [fevers], without doubt.

children.text: vyāyāmaṃ ca vyavāyaṃ ca snānaṃ caṅkramaṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Exercise, sexual intercourse, bathing, and walking —

children.text: jvaramukto na seveta yāvanno balavānbhavet // Rmañj_6.66 //
children.translated_text: one freed from fever should not engage in these until one has become strong.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ tathā gandhaṃ mṛtābhraṃ viṣasaṃyutam // Rmañj_6.67 //
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, sulphur, killed mica, combined with poison —
in equal parts, the wise one should grind them with juices of <s>tālamūlī</s> for three days.
Having filled a flask with that, sealing it, and drying it,
having wrapped it with seven layers of clay-cloth, one should then dry it.
One should calcine it with a pot-sized [fire]; when cooled naturally, one should take it out.
Having taken it from the middle of the flask, one should then grind it for one day.

children.text: ajājīcitrakaṃ hiṅgu svarjikā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca yat // Rmañj_6.70 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ajājī</s> (cumin), <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>svarjikā</s> (soda ash), and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
<s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), five salts, <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali), and <s>yavānikā</s> (bishop's weed),

children.text: maricaṃ pippalī caiva pratyekaṃ ca samānataḥ // Rmañj_6.71 //
children.translated_text: pepper and <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) — each in equal proportion —
with the decoction of these, one should treat [the preparation] again, seven times in sunlight.
With a <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel) leaf, five-<s>guñjā</s> [dose] of this Lord of Mercury
should be given in severe new fever; warm water should be drunk afterward.
This preparation called <s>Prāṇeśvara</s> is the remover of <s>sannipāta</s> (combined disorder of all three <s>doṣas</s>).
In cold fever, fever preceded by burning, abdominal lump (<s>gulma</s>), colic arising from the three <s>doṣas</s>,
the desired food should be given; one should apply sandalwood paste.
The excessive heat is pacified by conversation with children and singing;

children.text: prabhavennātra sandehaḥ svāsthyaṃ ca labhate naraḥ // Rmañj_6.75 //
children.translated_text: there is no doubt that health is attained — the person recovers.
<s>Navajvarebhasiṃha Rasa</s> (Lion against New Fever)

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ tathā gandhaṃ lohaṃ tāmraṃ ca sīsakam /
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, sulphur, iron, copper, and lead,

children.text: maricaṃ pippalīṃ viśvaṃ samabhāgāni cūrṇayet // Rmañj_6.76 //
children.translated_text: pepper, <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>viśva</s> (dry ginger) — all in equal parts should be powdered.
Having added half a part of poison (<s>viṣa</s>), one should grind for two days;
with fresh ginger as the vehicle, the physician should give a two-<s>guñjā</s> dose.
In severe new fever, in <s>vāta</s> (wind) diseases, in <s>saṃgrahaṇī</s> (dysentery) —
this <s>Navajvarebhasiṃha</s> should be employed in all diseases.
<s>Pañcānana Jvarāṅkuśa Rasa</s> (Five-faced Fever-goad)

children.text: śambhoḥ kaṇṭhavibhūṣaṇaṃ samaricaṃ mārāriraktaṃ raviḥ pakṣau sāgaralocanaṃ śaśiyutaṃ bhāgo'rkasaṃkhyānvitam /
children.translated_text: The ornament of <s>Śambhu's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) throat [i.e., poison] with pepper, the blood of the enemy of <s>Māra</s> [i.e., realgar]; the sun [i.e., twelve parts]; the two wings [i.e., two parts]; the ocean-eye [i.e., four parts]; combined with the moon [i.e., one part]; the share numbered as the sun [i.e., twelve] —

children.text: khalve taṃ khalu marditaṃ ravijalair guñjaikamātraṃ tataḥ siddho'yaṃ jvaradantadarpadalanaḥ pañcānanākhyo rasaḥ // Rmañj_6.79 //
children.translated_text: that ground well in a mortar with sun-water [fresh ginger juice], one <s>guñjā</s> measure — thus perfected, this preparation called <s>Pañcānana</s> (Five-faced) crushes the pride of the tooth [i.e., the sharp bite] of fever.

children.text: pathyaṃ ca deyaṃ dadhitakrabhaktaṃ sindhūtthayuktaṃ sitayā sametam /
children.translated_text: The prescribed diet should be yogurt, buttermilk, and rice, combined with <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) and sugar;

children.text: gandhānulepo himatoyapānaṃ dugdhaṃ ca deyaṃ śubhadāḍimaṃ ca // Rmañj_6.80 //
children.translated_text: sandalwood paste should be applied, cold water should be drunk, and milk and auspicious pomegranate should be given.
<s>Pañcānana Rasa</s> (Five-faced Preparation)

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhakacitrakaṃ trikaṭukaṃ mustā viṣaṃ traiphalam etebhyo dviguṇāṃ guḍena guṭikāṃ guṃjāpramāṇāṃ haret /
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulphur, <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>), <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus), poison, and the three fruits (<s>triphala</s>) — from these, pills twice [the size], with jaggery, of <s>guñjā</s> measure, should be made.

children.text: kuṣṭhāṣṭādaśa vāyuśūlamudaraṃ śoṣapramehādikaṃ rogānīkakarīndradarpadalane khyāto hi pañcānanaḥ // Rmañj_6.81 //
children.translated_text: Eighteen types of leprosy, <s>vāta</s>-colic, abdominal tumors, consumption, urinary disorders, etc. — in crushing the pride of the elephant of the host of diseases, this <s>Pañcānana</s> (Five-faced) is renowned.
<s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī Rasa</s> (Reviver of the Dead)
Four parts of <s>mleccha</s> (cinnabar/foreign mercury), three parts of <s>jaipāla</s> (croton) are prescribed,

children.text: dvau bhāgau ṭaṅkaṇasyaiva bhāgaikamamṛtasya ca // Rmañj_6.82 //
children.translated_text: two parts of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and one part of <s>amṛta</s> (Tinospora cordifolia).

children.text: tatsarvaṃ mardayet sūkṣmaṃ śuṣkaṃ yāmaṃ bhiṣagvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The best physician should grind all of this finely, dry, for one <s>yāma</s> (watch);
with ginger-water it should be given, along with <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), <s>citraka</s>, and <s>saindhava</s>;
two <s>guñjā</s> in measure — this certainly removes the burning [fever].

body.translated_text: One should apply sandalwood paste combined with camphor.

children.translated_text: The physician should revive the patient with a bronze vessel [for fanning];
<s>śāli</s> rice with buttermilk should be fed, combined with <s>bilva</s> (wood apple).
In terrible <s>sannipāta</s> (combined disorder), in fever from the three <s>doṣas</s>, in irregular fever,

children.text: āmavāte vātaśūle gulme plīhni jalodare // Rmañj_6.86 //
children.translated_text: in <s>āmavāta</s> (rheumatism), <s>vāta</s>-colic, abdominal lump, splenic disorder, and ascites,
in [fever] preceded by cold, [fever] preceded by burning, in irregular and continuous fever,

children.text: agnimāṃdye ca vāte ca prayojyo'yaṃ raseśvaraḥ // Rmañj_6.87 //
children.translated_text: in weak digestive fire and in <s>vāta</s> disorders — this Lord of Mercury should be employed.

body.translated_text: This is known as <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvana</s> (Reviver of the Dead) in the ocean of mercury [literature].

children.translated_text: <s>Ravisundara Rasa</s> (Beautiful Sun Preparation)

children.text: dvibhāgatālena hataṃ ca tāmraṃ rasaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca viṣaṃ samaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Copper killed with double-portion <s>tāla</s> (orpiment); mercury, sulphur, and poison in equal [parts];

children.text: jayapālabījaṃ dviguṇaṃ ca dadyāt trisaptavāreṇa divākarāṃśau // Rmañj_6.89 //
children.translated_text: <s>jayapāla</s> (croton) seed should be given in double quantity — [ground] twenty-one times with the rays of the sun [i.e., in sunlight].

children.text: vimardya nimbasvarasena cūrṇaṃ guñjaikamānaṃ sitayā sametam /
children.translated_text: Having ground it with neem juice into powder, one <s>guñjā</s> measure combined with sugar —
this fever-goad called <s>Ravisundara</s> destroys all eight types of fever completely.
<s>Sannipāta Bhairava Rasa</s> (Fearsome Preparation for Combined Disorders)
Copper, sulphur, mercury, <s>śveta</s> (white lead?), <s>spandā</s> (?), pepper, and <s>pūtanā</s> (?),
<s>samīna</s> (?), <s>pitta</s> (bile-salt?), and <s>jaipāla</s> (croton) — all equal, ground together.
Four <s>guñjā</s> of this — it is the supreme destroyer of new fever;
this fever-goad called <s>Sannipāta Bhairava</s> has been proclaimed.
<s>Bhasmeśvara Rasa</s> (Lord of Ashes Preparation)
The <s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash) should be sixteen <s>niṣkas</s> in quantity, produced from wild stone;

children.text: niṣkatrayaṃ ca maricaṃ viṣaṃ niṣkaṃ ca cūrṇayet // Rmañj_6.93 //
children.translated_text: three <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>marica</s> (black pepper) and one <s>niṣka</s> of <s>viṣa</s> (aconite) should be powdered. // Rmañj_6.93 //
This [preparation] named <s>Bhasmeśvara</s> is a destroyer of <s>sannipāta</s> (tri-doṣic fever);
one should consume five <s>guñjā</s>-measures with the juice of fresh ginger. // Rmañj_6.94 //
<s>Pratāpalaṅkeśvara Rasa</s>
The powder of the root of <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera), together with the bark from the root of <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago zeylanica),

children.text: valkalairmardayitvā ca rasaṃ vastreṇa gālayet // Rmañj_6.95 //
children.translated_text: having ground [them together], one should strain the juice through a cloth. // Rmañj_6.95 //
With that [juice], mercury, an equal amount of <s>gandha</s> (sulphur), <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>darada</s> (cinnabar), <s>viṣa</s> (aconite),

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tālakaṃ caiva mardayed dinasaptakam // Rmañj_6.96 //
children.translated_text: <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) should be ground for seven days. // Rmañj_6.96 //
For three days it should be levigated with the tubers of <s>muśalī</s> (Curculigo orchioides), kept protected from heat;
filling a cow-udder-shaped crucible, one should seal it all around. // Rmañj_6.97 //
Having wrapped it with seven layers of clay and cloth, it should be given a light <s>puṭa</s> (calcination firing).

children.text: rasatulyaṃ lohavaṅgau rajataṃ tāmrakaṃ tathā // Rmañj_6.98 //
children.translated_text: Equal to the mercury [in quantity], iron and tin, silver, and copper likewise, // Rmañj_6.98 //
<s>madhūka</s> (Madhuca indica) extract and water, <s>reṇukā</s> (Vitex agnus-castus), <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin), <s>śilā</s> (realgar),

children.text: cavyakaṃ ca samāṃśaṃ syādbhāgārddhaṃ śodhitaṃ viṣam // Rmañj_6.99 //
children.translated_text: and <s>cavyaka</s> (Piper chaba) in equal parts, and purified <s>viṣa</s> (aconite) in half part. // Rmañj_6.99 //
All that should be ground in a mortar, and levigated with the juice of <s>viṣa</s> (aconite);

children.text: ātape saptadhā tīvre mardayed ghaṭikādvayam // Rmañj_6.100 //
children.translated_text: it should be ground seven times in intense sunlight for two <s>ghaṭikās</s> (48 minutes). // Rmañj_6.100 //
With a decoction of the three pungents (<s>kaṭutraya</s>), and with the juice of <s>kanaka</s> (Datura metel),
with a decoction of the three fruits (<s>phalatraya</s> / <s>triphalā</s>), and with the juice of <s>munipuṣpa</s> (Agasti), // Rmañj_6.101 //
with the juice of <s>samudraphala</s> (Barringtonia acutangula), and with the water of <s>vijayā</s> (Cannabis),

children.text: citrakasya kaṣāyeṇa jvālāmukhyā rasena ca // Rmañj_6.102 //
children.translated_text: with a decoction of <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago zeylanica), and with the juice of <s>jvālāmukhī</s> (Gloriosa superba), // Rmañj_6.102 //

children.text: pratyekaṃ saptadhā bhāvyaṃ tadvatpiṣṭaṃ ca bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: it should be levigated seven times with each [of these]; similarly the paste should be levigated
with an equal portion of all [juices combined], and fumigated with <s>viṣa</s> (aconite). // Rmañj_6.103 //
Having ground it for a day, one should store it in a small bottle;
one <s>guñjā</s>-measure [should be given] with hot water or with the juice of fresh ginger. // Rmañj_6.104 //
It should be given to the patient for the pacification of severe unconsciousness and loss of memory;
having struck the palate with an instrument, one should rub it with fresh juice. // Rmañj_6.105 //
When the teeth do not open, then one should perform this procedure:
one should sprinkle [the patient] repeatedly with a hundred pots of water after reciting mantras. // Rmañj_6.106 //
When the desire for food arises in that patient, then
one should give rice with yogurt mixed with sugar, and buttermilk with cumin. // Rmañj_6.107 //

children.text: pāne pānaṃ sitāyuktaṃ yadīcchati tadā dadet /
children.translated_text: If [the patient] desires a drink, one should give a beverage mixed with sugar;

children.text: evaṃ kṛte na śāntiḥ syāttāpasya rasajasya ca // Rmañj_6.108 //
children.translated_text: when this is done, the heat caused by the <s>rasa</s> (mercurial preparation) does not subside [merely by these means]. // Rmañj_6.108 //
One should apply a cooling paste of camphor and sandalwood juice;
a bed should be surrounded with cotton, jasmine, <s>jātī</s> (Jasminum grandiflorum), <s>punnāga</s> (Calophyllum inophyllum), and <s>bakula</s> (Mimusops elengi) [flowers]. // Rmañj_6.109 //
Having prepared such a bed, one should repeatedly anoint the [patient] resting there with sandalwood;
with coquettish gestures, graceful movements, playful words, sidelong glances, and restless eyes, // Rmañj_6.110 //
with the pressing of full and high breasts, with the embraces of beautiful women,
with the pleasant sounds of the <s>vīṇā</s> and other [instruments], and with songs that are nectar to the ears, // Rmañj_6.111 //
with auspicious conversations about stories from the sacred <s>Purāṇas</s> —

children.text: ebhiḥ prakāraistāpasya jāyate śamanaṃ param // Rmañj_6.112 //
children.translated_text: by these means, the supreme pacification of the [mercury-induced] heat is achieved. // Rmañj_6.112 //
One should avoid sexual intercourse until [the patient] becomes strong again;
in diseases beginning with <s>vāta</s>, it should be given with rock salt, <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), and <s>vahni</s> (dry ginger). // Rmañj_6.113 //
It should be given with <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper) and honey in <s>kāmalā</s> (jaundice), <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption), and <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anaemia);
it should be employed in all diseases with the appropriate <s>anupāna</s> (vehicle) for each disease. // Rmañj_6.114 //

body.translated_text: This <s>Pratāpalaṅkeśa</s> [Rasa] is a destroyer of <s>sannipāta</s> (tri-doṣic fever). // Rmañj_6.115 //

children.translated_text: <s>Mahodadhi Rasa</s>

children.text: sūtakaṃ gandhakaṃ lohaṃ viṣaṃ cāpi varāṭakam /
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulphur, iron, <s>viṣa</s> (aconite), and <s>varāṭaka</s> (cowrie-shell ash),

children.text: tāmrakaṃ vaṅgabhasmātha abhrakaṃ ca samāṃśakam // Rmañj_6.116 //
children.translated_text: copper, <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) <s>bhasma</s> (ash), and <s>abhraka</s> (mica) — all in equal parts; // Rmañj_6.116 //
<s>trikaṭu</s> (the three pungents), <s>patra</s> (Cinnamomum tamala leaf), <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus rotundus), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), <s>nāgakeśara</s> (Mesua ferrea),
<s>reṇukā</s> (Vitex agnus-castus), <s>āmalaka</s> (Phyllanthus emblica), and <s>pippalīmūla</s> (long pepper root) as well; // Rmañj_6.117 //

children.text: eṣāṃ ca dviguṇaṃ bhāgaṃ mardayitvā prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: twice the quantity of these [herbal ingredients] should be carefully ground;
levigation should be given with the water of <s>gajapippalī</s> (Scindapsus officinalis). // Rmañj_6.118 //
The dose is the size of a chickpea — this pill is prescribed;

children.text: śvāsaṃ hanti tathā kāsam arśāṃsi ca bhagandaram // Rmañj_6.119 //
children.translated_text: it destroys <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnoea), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>arśas</s> (haemorrhoids), and <s>bhagandara</s> (fistula-in-ano); // Rmañj_6.119 //
<s>hṛcchūla</s> (cardiac pain), <s>pārśvaśūla</s> (pain in the sides), <s>karṇaroga</s> (ear disease), and headache;
it removes <s>saṃgrahaṇīroga</s> (malabsorption disorder), and the eight types of abdominal diseases,

children.text: pramehaviṃśatiṃ caiva aśmarīṃ ca caturvidhām // Rmañj_6.120 //
children.translated_text: as well as the twenty types of <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders) and four types of <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary calculi). // Rmañj_6.120 //

children.text: na cānnapāne parihāramasti na śītavātādhvani maithune ca /
children.translated_text: There is no restriction in food and drink, nor [avoidance of] cold, wind, travel, or sexual intercourse;
engaged in whatever activities one desires during the course of treatment, a man becomes radiant like a heap of gold. // Rmañj_6.121 //
<s>Madodadhi Vaṭī</s>

children.text: ekaikaṃ viṣasūtaṃ ca jātī ṭaṅkaṃ dvikaṃ dvikam /
children.translated_text: One part each of <s>viṣa</s> (aconite) and mercury, two parts each of <s>jātī</s> (nutmeg) and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
three parts of <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (long pepper), six parts of <s>viśva</s> (dry ginger), and two parts of calcined <s>kapardikā</s> (cowrie shell); // Rmañj_6.122 //
five parts of <s>devapuṣpa</s> (clove) — all should be ground together carefully;
the pill called <s>Mahodadhi</s> kindles the extinguished digestive fire. // Rmañj_6.123 //
<s>Unmatta Rasa</s>

children.text: rasaṃ ca gandhakaṃ caiva dhattūraphalajair dravaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury and sulphur should be ground with the juices of <s>dhattūra</s> (Datura stramonium) fruits

children.text: mardayed dinamekaṃ ca tulyaṃ trikaṭukaṃ kṣipet // Rmañj_6.124 //
children.translated_text: for one day, and an equal amount of <s>trikaṭuka</s> (the three pungents) should be added. // Rmañj_6.124 //
The [preparation] named <s>Unmatta Rasa</s> is a destroyer of <s>sannipāta</s> (tri-doṣic fever);

children.text: kastena na kṛto dharmaḥ kāṃ ca pūjāṃ na so'rhati /
children.translated_text: what meritorious act has not been performed by him, and what worship does he not deserve,
who rescues an embodied being drowned in the ocean of <s>sannipāta</s>? // Rmañj_6.125 //
<s>Saṃjñākaraṇa Rasa</s>
<s>Vacā</s> (Acorus calamus), garlic, <s>kaṭuka</s> (Picrorhiza kurroa), <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>bṛhatīphala</s> (fruit of Solanum indicum),

children.text: rudrākṣaṃ madhusāraṃ ca phalaṃ sāmudrakāmṛtam // Rmañj_6.126 //
children.translated_text: <s>rudrākṣa</s> (Elaeocarpus ganitrus), <s>madhusāra</s> (honey extract), <s>sāmudra</s> (sea salt) fruit, and <s>amṛta</s> (Tinospora cordifolia); // Rmañj_6.126 //
these in equal parts should be levigated with the milk of <s>arka</s> (Calotropis gigantea);
they should be levigated with fish bile three times and then powdered. // Rmañj_6.127 //
This insufflation (<s>dhamana</s>) is declared supreme in severe <s>sannipāta</s>,
in <s>kapha</s>-dominant [conditions], in excessive <s>vāta</s>, in <s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy), and in <s>halīmaka</s> (advanced jaundice); // Rmañj_6.128 //
in diseases of the head, in ear diseases, and in eye diseases, as per the prescribed method,
it should be administered through the two nostrils — this is the excellent <s>Saṃjñākaraṇa</s> (consciousness-restorer). // Rmañj_6.129 //

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ samaṃ gandhaṃ maricaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tathā // Rmañj_6.130 //
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, an equal amount of sulphur, <s>marica</s> (black pepper), and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) likewise; // Rmañj_6.130 //
four times as much sugar should be added, and it should be levigated with fish bile;
it should be ground for three days — this <s>rasa</s> is [called] <s>Candraśekhara</s>. // Rmañj_6.131 //
Two <s>guñjā</s>-measures should be given with ginger juice, followed by cold water;

children.text: takrabhaktaṃ ca vṛntākaṃ pathyaṃ tatra nidhāpayet // Rmañj_6.132 //
children.translated_text: buttermilk-rice and <s>vṛntāka</s> (brinjal) should be prescribed as the dietary regimen. // Rmañj_6.132 //

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ maricaṃ gandhaṃ pippalīṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ viṣam // Rmañj_6.133 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), <s>marica</s> (black pepper), <s>gandha</s> (sulphur), <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>viṣa</s> (aconite); // Rmañj_6.133 //
and the seeds of <s>kanaka</s> (Datura metel), in equal parts, with the juices of <s>vijayā</s> (Cannabis),

children.text: mardayedyāmamātraṃ tu caṇamātrā vaṭī kṛtā // Rmañj_6.134 //
children.translated_text: should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours), and pills the size of a chickpea should be made. // Rmañj_6.134 //
By consuming it, the <s>rasa</s> [called] <s>Kanakasundara</s> destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption);

children.text: agnimāṃdyaṃ jvaraṃ tīvramatisāraṃ ca nāśayet // Rmañj_6.135 //
children.translated_text: it removes <s>agnimāndya</s> (digestive weakness), severe <s>jvara</s> (fever), and <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhoea). // Rmañj_6.135 //
For those afflicted with <s>grahaṇī</s> disorders, buttermilk is digestive-kindling, absorbent, and light;
it is wholesome due to its sweet post-digestive effect, and does not aggravate <s>pitta</s>. // Rmañj_6.136 //

children.text: sūtakaṃ gandhakaṃ caiva śāṇaṃ śāṇaṃ ca gṛhyate // Rmañj_6.137 //
children.translated_text: Mercury and sulphur are taken, one <s>śāṇa</s> each; // Rmañj_6.137 //

children.text: daradaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ caiva maricaṃ ca viṣaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Darada</s> (cinnabar), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>marica</s> (black pepper), and <s>viṣa</s> (aconite) —

children.text: catvāra auṣadhayaḥ sarve dvidviṭaṅkaṃ ca kathyate // Rmañj_6.138 //
children.translated_text: all these four medicines are stated as two <s>ṭaṅkas</s> each. // Rmañj_6.138 //
The seed of <s>jaipāla</s> (Croton tiglium) should be combined, [measuring] one <s>ṭaṅka</s> per direction (i.e., ten <s>ṭaṅkas</s>);
it should be ground with tamarind juice and made into pills of one <s>guñjā</s> measure. // Rmañj_6.139 //
Combined with <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil) leaves, all types of irregular fevers —

children.text: aikāhikaṃ dvyāhikaṃ ca tryāhikaṃ ca caturthakam // Rmañj_6.140 //
children.translated_text: quotidian, tertian, quartan, and <s>caturthaka</s> (every fourth day), // Rmañj_6.140 //
all [fevers] beginning with chills and burning — it destroys rapidly;

children.text: pathyaṃ dugdhaudanaṃ deyaṃ dadhibhaktaṃ ca bhojanam // Rmañj_6.141 //
children.translated_text: milk-rice and yogurt-rice should be given as the dietary regimen. // Rmañj_6.141 //

body.translated_text: The [preparation] named <s>Rāmavāṇa Rasa</s> is the destroyer of all diseases. // Rmañj_6.142 //

children.translated_text: <s>Candraprabhā Vaṭī</s>

children.text: mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ mṛtaṃ tāmraṃ mṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ samaṃ samam /
children.translated_text: Calcined mercury, calcined copper, and calcined gold, in equal parts,

children.text: tulyaṃ ca khādiraṃ sāraṃ tathā mocarasaṃ kṣipet // Rmañj_6.143 //
children.translated_text: and an equal quantity of <s>khādira</s> (Acacia catechu) heartwood extract, and <s>mocarasa</s> (silk-cotton tree resin) should be added. // Rmañj_6.143 //
With the juices extracted from <s>śālmalī</s> (Bombax ceiba) root, it should be ground for two <s>praharas</s> (six hours);
a pill the size of a chickpea should be consumed, [measuring] one <s>niṣka</s>, together with cumin;
it surely destroys <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhoea) arising from all three <s>doṣas</s>, along with fever. // Rmañj_6.144 //
<s>Citrāmbara Rasa</s>
Purified mercury, calcined <s>abhraka</s> (mica), and sulphur should be ground in equal parts;

children.text: lohapātre ghṛtābhyakte yāmaṃ mṛdvagninā pacet // Rmañj_6.145 //
children.translated_text: in an iron vessel smeared with ghee, it should be cooked over mild fire for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours). // Rmañj_6.145 //
It should be stirred with an iron rod, then removed and examined;

children.text: tridinaṃ jīrakaiḥ kvāthair māsaikaṃ bhakṣayennaraḥ // Rmañj_6.146 //
children.translated_text: a man should consume it for three days with cumin decoction, and for one month. // Rmañj_6.146 //
The <s>rasa</s> named <s>Citrāmbara</s> cures <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption) accompanied with bleeding;
with the [appropriate] <s>anupāna</s> (vehicle), it cures <s>āmaśūla</s> (gastric pain from undigested food) and <s>pravāhikā</s> (dysentery). // Rmañj_6.147 //
<s>Grahaṇīkapāṭa Rasa</s>
Silver, pearl, gold, and iron — each one part;
sulphur two parts, mercury three parts — these should be ground for a day. // Rmañj_6.148 //
Firmly [triturated] with the juice of <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple), then placed into a deer-horn [crucible];
after a medium <s>puṭa</s> (calcination firing), it should be taken out and ground again. // Rmañj_6.149 //
Seven times with the juices of <s>balā</s> (Sida cordifolia), and three times with the juices of <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera);

<s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos racemosa), <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum heterophyllum), <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus rotundus), <s>dhātakī</s> (Woodfordia fruticosa), <s>indrayava</s> (Holarrhena seeds), and <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora cordifolia) — // Rmañj_6.150 //
with the fresh juice of each of these, levigation should be done three times each;

children.text: māṣamātraraso deyo madhunā maricaiḥ saha // Rmañj_6.151 //
children.translated_text: the <s>rasa</s> in the dose of one <s>māṣa</s> should be given with honey and black pepper. // Rmañj_6.151 //
It destroys all types of <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhoea) and the five types of <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption);
this <s>rasa</s> named <s>Kapāṭa</s> for <s>grahaṇī</s> also kindles the digestive fire. // Rmañj_6.152 //
<s>Grahaṇīkapāṭa Rasa</s> (method 2)
Pearl, gold, mercury, sulphur, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>kaparda</s> (cowrie-shell ash), and <s>amṛta</s> (Tinospora) — in equal parts;

children.text: sarvaiḥ samaṃ śaṅkhakacūrṇayuktaṃ khalve ca bhāvyo'tiviṣādraveṇa // Rmañj_6.153 //
children.translated_text: equal to all [of these combined], conch-shell powder should be added, and ground in a mortar with the juice of <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum heterophyllum). // Rmañj_6.153 //

children.text: golaṃ ca kṛtvā mṛtkarpaṭasthaṃ saṃrudhya bhāṇḍe hi paced dinārdham /
children.translated_text: Having made a ball and placed it on a clay potsherd, it should be sealed in a vessel and cooked for half a day;

children.text: susvāṅgaśīto rasa eṣa bhāvyo dhattūravahṇimuśalīdravaiśca // Rmañj_6.154 //
children.translated_text: when completely self-cooled, this <s>rasa</s> should be levigated with the juices of <s>dhattūra</s> (Datura), <s>vahni</s> (Plumbago), and <s>muśalī</s> (Curculigo). // Rmañj_6.154 //

children.text: lohasya pātre paripācitaśca siddho bhavet saṃgrahaṇīkapāṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Cooked in an iron vessel, it becomes the perfected <s>Saṃgrahaṇīkapāṭa</s>;
in <s>vāta</s>-dominant [grahaṇī], it should be taken with black pepper and ghee; in <s>pitta</s>-dominant, with honey and long pepper; // Rmañj_6.155 //

body.text: śleṣmottarāyāṃ vijayārasena kaṭutrayeṇāpi yuto grahaṇyām // Rmañj_6.156 //
body.translated_text: in <s>kapha</s>-dominant, with the juice of <s>vijayā</s> (Cannabis); combined with the three pungents in [general] <s>grahaṇī</s>. // Rmañj_6.156 //

children.translated_text: In <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption), fever, haemorrhoids, faecal disorders, <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhoea) with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter), loss of appetite, and rhinitis,

children.text: mohe ca kṛcchre gatadhātuvṛddhau guñjādvayaṃ cāpi mahāmayaghnam // Rmañj_6.157 //
children.translated_text: in stupor, dysuria, and loss of <s>dhātu</s> (bodily tissues) — two <s>guñjā</s>-measures destroy great diseases. // Rmañj_6.157 //
Calcined mercury, <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>gandha</s> (sulphur), <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali), and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax); // Rmañj_6.158 //

children.text: agnimanthaṃ vacāṃ kuryāt sūtatulyām imāṃ sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: the wise one should add <s>agnimantha</s> (Premna integrifolia) and <s>vacā</s> (Acorus calamus) equal to the mercury;
then it should be ground with the juices of <s>jayantī</s> (Sesbania sesban), <s>jambīra</s> (citron), and <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta alba). // Rmañj_6.159 //

children.text: trivāsaraṃ tato golaṃ kṛtvā saṃśoṣya dhārayet /
children.translated_text: For three days; then having made a ball and dried it, one should keep it;

children.text: lohapātre ca lavaṇaṃ athopari nidhāpayet // Rmañj_6.160 //
children.translated_text: in an iron vessel, salt should be placed, and [the ball placed] upon it. // Rmañj_6.160 //

children.text: adhovahniṃ śanaiḥ kuryād yāmārdhaṃ ca tad uddharet /
children.translated_text: One should apply gentle fire from below for half a <s>yāma</s> (one and a half hours), then take it out;
<s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum heterophyllum) equal to the mercury should be added, and likewise <s>mocarasa</s> (silk-cotton resin). // Rmañj_6.161 //
The physician should levigated it seven times with the juices of <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) and <s>vijayā</s> (Cannabis);

<s>dhātakī</s> (Woodfordia fruticosa), <s>indrayava</s> (Holarrhena seeds), <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus rotundus), <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos racemosa), <s>bilva</s> (Aegle marmelos), and <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora cordifolia); // Rmañj_6.162 //
having levigated with the juices of these, it should be dried once;

children.text: rasavajraṃ kapāṭākhyaṃ māṣaikaṃ madhunā lihet // Rmañj_6.163 //
children.translated_text: this <s>rasa</s> called <s>Vajrakapāṭa</s> — one <s>māṣa</s> should be licked with honey. // Rmañj_6.163 //

children.text: vahniḥ śuṇṭhī viḍaṅgāpi bilvaṃ ca lavaṇaṃ samam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vahni</s> (dry ginger), <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), <s>bilva</s> (Aegle marmelos), and salt in equal parts;

children.text: pibed uṣṇāmbunā cānu sarvajāṃ grahaṇīṃ jayet // Rmañj_6.164 //
children.translated_text: one should drink with warm water afterwards — it conquers all types of <s>grahaṇī</s>. // Rmañj_6.164 //
<s>Vijayabhairava Rasa</s>
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), <s>loha</s> (iron), <s>viṣa</s> (poison/aconite), <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago zeylanica), <s>abhraka</s> (ite),
<s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), <s>reṇukā</s>, <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus rotundus), <s>elā</s> (cardamom), <s>keśara</s> (saffron), <s>patraka</s> (cinnamon leaf),

children.text: phalatrayaṃ trikaṭukaṃ śulbabhasma tathaiva ca // Rmañj_6.165 //
children.translated_text: <s>phalatraya</s> (the three fruits — Terminalia chebula, Terminalia bellirica, and Emblica officinalis), <s>trikaṭuka</s> (the three pungents — ginger, pepper, and long pepper), and likewise <s>śulba</s> (copper) ash. [Rmañj 6.165]
All these in equal parts, with double the quantity of <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) added;

children.text: kāse śvāse kṣaye gulme pramehe viṣamajvare // Rmañj_6.166 //
children.translated_text: [It is effective] in <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), and irregular fevers. [Rmañj 6.166]
In puerperal [diseases], <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), sluggishness, <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), and likewise
in diseases of the hands, feet, etc. — this pill is recommended. [Rmañj 6.167]

children.text: daradaṃ vatsanābhaṃ ca maricaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kaṇā // Rmañj_6.168 //
children.translated_text: <s>Darada</s> (cinnabar), <s>vatsanābha</s> (aconite), <s>marica</s> (black pepper), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper) — [Rmañj 6.168]
these should be powdered in equal parts; this <s>rasa</s> is indeed <s>Ānandabhairava</s>.

children.text: guñjaikaṃ tu dviguñjaṃ vā balaṃ jñātvā prayojayet // Rmañj_6.169 //
children.translated_text: One <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed weight, ~0.12g) or two <s>guñjā</s> doses should be administered after assessing the patient's strength. [Rmañj 6.169]
Afterward, one should lick with honey the powdered fruit-rind of <s>kuṭaja</s> (Holarrhena antidysenterica),
in the measure of one <s>karṣa</s> (12g) — it conquers diarrhea of all three <s>doṣas</s>. [Rmañj 6.170]
As diet, one should give rice with yogurt, and goat's buttermilk;

children.text: pipāsāyāṃ jalaṃ śītaṃ hitā ca vijayā niśi // Rmañj_6.171 //
children.translated_text: when thirsty, cold water [should be given], and <s>vijayā</s> (cannabis/bhang) is beneficial at night. [Rmañj 6.171]
<Meghaḍambara Rasa>
<s>Gandhaka</s> (sulphur) in equal quantity to mercury, ground with the juice of <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus),

children.text: andhamūṣāgataṃ paktvā bhūdhare bhasmatāṃ nayet // Rmañj_6.172 //
children.translated_text: should be placed in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>) and cooked, then reduced to ash in an earth-furnace (<s>bhūdhara</s>). [Rmañj 6.172]
It should be processed with decoction of <s>daśamūla</s> (ten roots) for two <s>praharas</s> (six hours).

children.text: guñjādvayaṃ haratyāśu hikkāṃ kāsaṃ jvaraṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Two <s>guñjā</s> doses quickly destroy hiccups, cough, and fever;
this <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Meghaḍambara</s>, should be given with an appropriate vehicle (<s>anupāna</s>). [Rmañj 6.173]

children.text: gandhakād dviguṇaṃ sūtaṃ śuddhaṃ mṛdvagninā kṣaṇam // Rmañj_6.174 //
children.translated_text: Pure mercury in double the quantity of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), [heated] momentarily with gentle fire — [Rmañj 6.174]
after cooking, removing, and grinding, [it should be] mixed with <s>abhayā</s> (Terminalia chebula) powder in equal quantity.
One should eat seven <s>guñjā</s> [measure] and increase [the dose] day by day, [Rmañj 6.175]
by one <s>guñjā</s> gradually, until it reaches twenty-one.
The prescribed diet should be rice mixed with milk, ghee, and sugar. [Rmañj 6.176]
For the pacification of tremor-producing <s>vāta</s>, one should always dwell in a windless place.
The <s>rasa</s> named <s>Triguṇa</s> cures tremor-<s>vāta</s> within three fortnights. [Rmañj 6.177]
<Vātaripu Rasa>
Mercury, gold, diamond, silver, iron, and <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite),
<s>tāla</s> (orpiment), <s>nīlāñjana</s> (antimony), <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), and sea-foam — in equal parts; [Rmañj 6.178]
add one part of the five salts and triturate;

children.text: vajrakṣīrair dinaikaṃ tu ruddhvā taṃ bhūdhare puṭet // Rmañj_6.179 //
children.translated_text: seal with <s>vajra</s>-plant milk for one day, then calcine in an earth-furnace. [Rmañj 6.179]
One <s>māṣa</s> (1g) should be licked with fresh ginger juice — it destroys <s>vāta</s>;
a decoction made from <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) root should be administered as vehicle (<s>anupāna</s>) with black pepper. [Rmañj 6.180]
It destroys all <s>vāta</s> disorders including convulsions (<s>ākṣepaka</s>) and others;

children.text: rasaḥ sarvatra vikhyāto nāma vātaripuḥ smṛtaḥ // Rmañj_6.181 //
children.translated_text: this <s>rasa</s>, renowned everywhere, is known by the name <s>Vātaripu</s> (Enemy of Vāta). [Rmañj 6.181]
<Vātagajāṅkuśa Rasa>
Calcined iron, mercury-sulphur [amalgam], copper, orpiment, <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite),

children.text: pathyāṃ śṛṅgīviṣaṃ tryūṣam agnimanthaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇam // Rmañj_6.182 //
children.translated_text: <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>śṛṅgīviṣa</s> (aconite), <s>tryūṣa</s> (the three pungents), <s>agnimantha</s> (Premna integrifolia), and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) — [Rmañj 6.182]

children.text: tulyaṃ khalve dinaṃ mardya muṇḍīnirguṇḍijair dravaiḥ /
children.translated_text: in equal parts, ground in a mortar for one day with the juices of <s>muṇḍī</s> (Sphaeranthus indicus) and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo);
one should eat a pill of two <s>guñjā</s> measure for the pacification of all <s>vāta</s> [disorders].
The <s>Vātagajāṅkuśa</s> <s>rasa</s> quickly destroys both curable and incurable [diseases]. [Rmañj 6.183]
<Amlapittāntaka Rasa>
Equal parts of calcined mercury, <s>abhraka</s> (mica), and iron should be powdered with <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula);
three <s>māṣa</s> doses should be licked with honey for the pacification of <s>amlapitta</s> (hyperacidity). [Rmañj 6.184]
<Agnikumāra Rasa>

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ ca nāgānāṃ cūrṇaṃ haṃsāṅghrivāriṇā /
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulphur, and <s>nāga</s> (lead) powder [should be ground] with <s>haṃsāṅghri</s> (Adiantum) water

children.text: dinaṃ gharme vimardyātha golikāṃ tasya yojayet // Rmañj_6.185 //
children.translated_text: for one day in sunlight, and then a pill should be formed from it. [Rmañj 6.185]

children.text: kācakupyāṃ ca saṃveṣṭya tāṃ tribhir mṛtpuṭair dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Wrapping it in a glass flask, sealed firmly with three layers of clay coating,
closing the mouth and drying, it should be placed in a sand-bath (<s>sikatāhvaya</s>). [Rmañj 6.186]
One and a half days gradually, fire should be kindled beneath it;
when it has cooled by itself, extract it and add one-sixth part of <s>amṛta</s> (Tinospora cordifolia). [Rmañj 6.187]
Black pepper in half the proportion, mixed equally with <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda vasica), then triturated —
this is the <s>rasa</s> named <s>Agnikumāra</s>; its dose is one <s>raktikā</s> (guñjā measure). [Rmañj 6.188]
Combined with betel leaf juice, it destroys the following diseases:

children.text: vātarogān kṣayaṃ śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ pāṇḍukapholbaṇam // Rmañj_6.189 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vāta</s> diseases, consumption (<s>kṣaya</s>), dyspnea (<s>śvāsa</s>), cough (<s>kāsa</s>), severe anemia (<s>pāṇḍu</s>) and enlargement of the spleen (<s>kaphodara</s>), [Rmañj 6.189]
digestive weakness (<s>agnimāndya</s>), and <s>sannipāta</s> (disorders of all three humors). The prescribed diet is light food such as rice etc.
The application of water therapy is also recommended for the alleviation of heat. [Rmañj 6.190]
<Agnikumāra Rasa (variant)>

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ rasagandhau ca samabhāgaṃ trayo viṣam /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), mercury, and sulphur in equal parts — these three — with poison (<s>viṣa</s>),
<s>kapardi</s> (cowrie shell ash), <s>sarjikākṣāra</s> (sajji salt), <s>āgadhī</s> (long pepper), and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s> (dry ginger) — [Rmañj 6.191]
each in the measure of one <s>karṣa</s>, with one-eighth part of black pepper;
ground with citron juice for one day, this becomes <s>Agnikumāraka</s>,
for the alleviation of cholera (<s>viṣūcī</s>), colic (<s>śūla</s>), <s>vāta</s> disorders, and digestive weakness. [Rmañj 6.192]
<Līlāvilāsa Rasa>

children.text: raso ravirvyoma baliḥ sulohaṃ dhātryakṣanīraistridinaṃ vimardya /
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>rasa</s>), realgar (<s>ravi</s>), <s>vyoma</s> (mica), <s>bali</s> (tin), and good iron — ground for three days with <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) and <s>akṣa</s> (Terminalia bellirica) juices;

children.text: tadalpaghṛṣṭaṃ mṛdumārkaveṇa saṃmardayed asya ca vallayugmam // Rmañj_6.193 //
children.translated_text: that, lightly rubbed with mild sun[-heat], should then be thoroughly triturated, and two pills [formed] from it. [Rmañj 6.193]
Licked with honey, it destroys <s>amlapitta</s> (hyperacidity) — this is the <s>Līlāvilāsa</s>, king of <s>rasas</s>.

children.text: dugdhaṃ sakūṣmāṇḍarasaṃ sadhātrīphalaṃ śanaistatsahitaṃ bhajedvā // Rmañj_6.194 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, one may gradually take milk combined with ash-gourd juice, along with <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) fruit. [Rmañj 6.194]
<Manthānabhairava Rasa>
Calcined mercury, calcined copper, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>puṣkaramūla</s> (Inula racemosa root),

children.text: saindhavaṃ gandhakaṃ tālaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ cūrṇayetsamam // Rmañj_6.195 //
children.translated_text: <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), <s>tāla</s> (orpiment), and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) — powder in equal parts. [Rmañj 6.195]
With [juices of] <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa), <s>devadāru</s> (Cedrus deodara), <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo), <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus),
and bitter <s>kośātakī</s> (Luffa acutangula) juices, triturate firmly for one day. [Rmañj 6.196]
One <s>māṣa</s> dose should be licked with honey — this is the <s>Manthānabhairava</s> <s>rasa</s>.
For the alleviation of <s>kapha</s> diseases, one should drink <s>nimba</s> (neem) decoction afterward. [Rmañj 6.197]
<Kravyāda Rasa>

children.text: palaṃ rasasya dvipalaṃ baleḥ syācchulvāyasī cārdhapalapramāṇe /
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> (48g) of mercury, two <s>palas</s> of tin, and copper and iron each in half-<s>pala</s> measure;

children.text: saṃcūrṇya sarvaṃ drutam agniyogād eraṇḍapatreṣu niveśanīyam // Rmañj_6.198 //
children.translated_text: all should be powdered and quickly, by the application of fire, placed upon castor (<s>eraṇḍa</s>) leaves. [Rmañj 6.198]

children.text: piṣṭvātha tāṃ parpaṭikāṃ nidadhyāllohasya pātre varapūtam asmin /
children.translated_text: Then, having ground that wafer (<s>parpaṭikā</s>), one should place it in an iron vessel; in this [vessel],

children.text: jambīrajaṃ pakvarasaṃ palānāṃ śataṃ niyojyāgnimathāmlamātram // Rmañj_6.199 //
children.translated_text: add well-purified citron juice — one hundred <s>palas</s> — and then fire, with only the sour [liquid]. [Rmañj 6.199]
When the mercury is digested, it should be processed with these [juices] along with decoction of <s>pañcakola</s> (five spices) in full;

children.text: savetasāmlaiḥ śatamatra yojyaṃ samaṃ rajaṣ ṭaṃkaṇajaṃ subhṛṣṭam // Rmañj_6.200 //
children.translated_text: with <s>vetasa</s> (Calamus) sour [juice], one hundred [measures] should be added here, together with well-ground borax powder in equal proportion. [Rmañj 6.200]

children.text: viḍaṃ dadardhaṃ maricaṃ samaṃ ca tatsaptadhārdraṃ caṇakāmlavāri /
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍa</s> salt, half [quantity of] <s>darad</s> (cinnabar), and equal [measure of] pepper — these, moistened seven times with sour chickpea water;
the <s>rasa</s> well-known by the name <s>Kravyāda</s> (the Devourer) is described as in the <s>Manthānabhairava</s>.

children.text: māṣadvayaṃ saindhavatakrapītam etasudhanyaṃ khalu bhojanānte // Rmañj_6.201 //
children.translated_text: Two <s>māṣa</s> doses taken with rock salt and buttermilk, along with cooked grain — indeed at the end of a meal. [Rmañj 6.201]

children.text: gurūṇi māṃsāni payāṃsi piṣṭīghṛtāni khādyāni phalāni vegāt /
children.translated_text: Heavy meats, milk preparations, flour-based foods, ghee preparations, edible foods, and fruits —
even when consumed in excess, this renowned [<s>rasa</s>] digests them within two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours). [Rmañj 6.202]
<Agnituṇḍī Vaṭī (Pill)>
Purified mercury, poison (<s>viṣa</s>), sulphur, <s>ajamodā</s> (Apium graveolens), and the three fruits (<s>triphala</s>),
<s>sarjikṣāra</s> (sajji salt), <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali), fire-salt (<s>vahṇi</s>), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), and cumin (<s>jīraka</s>), [Rmañj 6.203]
<s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), sea salt, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) — in equal parts;
a fistful of poison, with all in equal measure, should be ground with citron juice. [Rmañj 6.204]

body.translated_text: One should eat a pill the size of a <s>marica</s> (pepper) for the alleviation of digestive weakness. [Rmañj 6.205]

children.translated_text: <Ānandodaya Rasa>
Mercury, sulphur, iron, mica, and likewise poison;

children.text: samāṃśaṃ maricaṃ cāṣṭau ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca caturguṇam // Rmañj_6.206 //
children.translated_text: equal parts of pepper, eight [parts], and borax in quadruple quantity — [Rmañj 6.206]
seven triturations with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta prostrata) juice, and [then] with sour pomegranate [juice];

children.text: guñjādvayaṃ parṇakhaṇḍairhanti sāyaṃ tu bhakṣitaḥ // Rmañj_6.207 //
children.translated_text: two <s>guñjā</s> [doses] with betel leaf pieces, eaten in the evening, destroy — [Rmañj 6.207]
diseases arising from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, digestive weakness, <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), fevers,
loss of appetite, and anemia — [all are] conquered by short-term use. [Rmañj 6.208]
<Cintāmaṇi Rasa>

children.text: rasaṃ gandhaṃ mṛtaṃ śulbaṃ mṛtamabhraṃ phalatrikam /
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulphur, calcined copper, calcined mica, and the three fruits,

children.text: tryūṣaṇaṃ bījajaipālaṃ samaṃ khalve vimardayet // Rmañj_6.209 //
children.translated_text: the three pungents (<s>tryūṣaṇa</s>), and <s>jaipāla</s> (Croton tiglium) seeds — grind equally in a mortar. [Rmañj 6.209]
It should be processed with <s>droṇapuṣpī</s> (Leucas cephalotes) juice, dried, and filtered through cloth.
This <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> <s>rasa</s> is recommended for cases of indigestion (<s>ajīrṇa</s>). [Rmañj 6.210]
It destroys eight types of fever and is praised in all [forms of] colic;

children.text: guñjaiko vā dviguṃjo vā āmarogaharaḥ paraḥ // Rmañj_6.211 //
children.translated_text: one <s>guñjā</s> or two <s>guñjā</s> doses — it is supreme in destroying <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) diseases. [Rmañj 6.211]
One <s>niṣka</s> (measure) each of mercury and sulphur; the digestive stimulant [in the same measure]; [Rmañj 6.212]
one and a half <s>palas</s> of <s>cūlikā</s> salt should be given; the physician
should triturate it in a mortar, then filter through a dry cloth. [Rmañj 6.213]
One <s>māṣa</s> dose should be given — it digests pearls, meat, etc.
In cases of indigestion and disorders of all three <s>doṣas</s>, this <s>Rājavallabha</s> should be administered. [Rmañj 6.214]
<Trinetra Rasa>

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ hāriṇaṃ śṛṅgaṃ svarṇaṃ śulbaṃ mṛtaṃ rasam /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>hāriṇa</s> (deer horn), horn (<s>śṛṅga</s>), gold, calcined copper, and mercury;
ground for one day with fresh ginger juice, sealed, and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed calcination). [Rmañj 6.215]
The <s>rasa</s> named <s>Trinetra</s> — one <s>māṣa</s> dose with honey and ghee.
Rock salt, cumin, and <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) should be licked afterward with honey and ghee;
it is renowned as a remedy for digestive colic — within one <s>yāma</s> (three hours), without doubt. [Rmañj 6.216]
<Mehavajra Rasa>

children.text: bhasma sūtaṃ mṛtaṃ kāntaṃ śulbabhasma śilājatu /
children.translated_text: Calcined mercury, calcined <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), copper ash, <s>śilājatu</s> (shilajit),
purified <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), rock (<s>śilā</s>), <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), and <s>aṅkola</s> (Alangium salviifolium) seeds, [Rmañj 6.217]
<s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple), <s>rajanī</s> (turmeric) powder — [all] should be processed with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta prostrata) [juice],
twenty times, dried, and then always licked with honey. [Rmañj 6.218]
One afflicted with <s>meha</s> (urinary disorder) should lick one <s>niṣka</s> measure; <s>Mehavajra</s> is a great <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: mahānimbasya bījāni piṣṭvā karṣamitāni ca // Rmañj_6.219 //
children.translated_text: The seeds of <s>mahānimba</s> (Melia azedarach), ground, in the measure of one <s>karṣa</s>, [Rmañj 6.219]
one <s>pala</s> with rice-water and two <s>niṣkas</s> of ghee —

children.text: ekīkṛtya pibettoyaṃ hanti mehaṃ cirotthitam // Rmañj_6.220 //
children.translated_text: combined together and drunk with water — it destroys long-standing <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders). [Rmañj 6.220]
<Indra Vaṭī Rasa>
Calcined mercury, calcined <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), combined with the bark of <s>Arjuna</s> (Terminalia arjuna),

children.text: tulyāṃśaṃ mardayet khalve śālmalyā mūlajair dravaiḥ // Rmañj_6.221 //
children.translated_text: in equal parts, ground in a mortar with juice from the roots of <s>śālmalī</s> (Bombax ceiba). [Rmañj 6.221]
At the end of the day, a pill of one <s>māṣa</s> measure should be made — it destroys <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders).
This is called <s>Indra Vaṭī</s> by name, for the alleviation of <s>madhumeha</s> (diabetes). [Rmañj 6.222]
<Rasendramaṅgala Rasa>

children.text: tālasattvaṃ mṛtaṃ tāmraṃ mṛtaṃ lohaṃ mṛtaṃ rasam /
children.translated_text: Essence of <s>tāla</s> (orpiment), calcined copper, calcined iron, calcined mercury,

children.text: hatamabhraṃ hataṃ tāraṃ gandhaṃ tutthaṃ manaḥśilā // Rmañj_6.223 //
children.translated_text: killed mica, killed silver, sulphur, <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), [Rmañj 6.223]
<s>sauvīrāñjana</s> (antimony), <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), <s>nīlī</s> (indigo), and <s>bhallātaka</s> (Semecarpus anacardium),
<s>śilājatu</s> (shilajit), <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) root, <s>kadalī</s> (plantain) tuber, and <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), [Rmañj 6.224]
bark of <s>aṅkola</s> (Alangium), black [variety], root of black <s>dhattūra</s> (Datura),
seeds of <s>avalguja</s> (Psoralea corylifolia), and fruits of <s>gaurī</s> and <s>mādhvī</s> (Madhuca), [Rmañj 6.225]
<s>hemāhvā</s> (Mesua ferrea), <s>phenajātī</s> (nutmeg), <s>phalinī</s> (Callicarpa), and <s>viṣatinduka</s> (Strychnos nux-vomica),

children.text: tailinyo lohakiṭṭaṃ ca purāṇamamṛtaṃ ca tat // Rmañj_6.226 //
children.translated_text: <s>tailinī</s> (sesame) and iron slag, and old <s>amṛta</s> (Tinospora cordifolia); [Rmañj 6.226]

children.text: tvacā ca mīnakākṣasya punaruktaṃ palaṃ pṛthak /
children.translated_text: also the bark of <s>mīnākṣa</s> (red bark tree) — each mentioned item, one <s>pala</s> separately.
The <s>tailinī</s> pills in those [quantities]; all should be powdered together. [Rmañj 6.227]

children.text: khalve nidhāya dātavyā punareṣāṃ ca bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Placed in a mortar, the [following] triturations should be given to these;

children.text: brahmadaṇḍī śikhāpuṅkhā devadālī ca nīlikā // Rmañj_6.228 //
children.translated_text: <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s> (Argemone mexicana), <s>śikhāpuṅkhā</s>, <s>devadālī</s> (Luffa echinata), and <s>nīlikā</s> (small indigo), [Rmañj 6.228]
<s>vāṇaśonā</s>, <s>nṛpataru</s> (royal tree), <s>nimba</s> (neem) essence, and <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica),
<s>karañja</s> (Pongamia pinnata), <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta prostrata), <s>gāyatrī</s>, and <s>tintaḍī</s> (tamarind) fruit, [Rmañj 6.229]
and root of <s>malayū</s> — three triturations each of these

children.text: dātavyā kuppikāṃ kṛtvā samyak saṃśoṣya cātape // Rmañj_6.230 //
children.translated_text: should be given; then, making a flask (<s>kuppikā</s>), it should be thoroughly dried in sunlight. [Rmañj 6.230]
One should place that vessel in [another] vessel and have it sealed;

children.text: yāmaṃ mandāgninā pacyāt puṭamadhye hyasau rasaḥ // Rmañj_6.231 //
children.translated_text: it should be cooked with gentle fire for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) within the <s>puṭa</s> (sealed calcination) — that is this <s>rasa</s>. [Rmañj 6.231]
It certainly destroys <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white leprosy/leucoderma) — there should be no doubt in this matter.

children.text: dvimāsābhyantare puṃsāmapathyaṃ na tu bhojayet // Rmañj_6.232 //
children.translated_text: One should not feed unwholesome food (<s>apathya</s>) to men within two months. // Rmañj_6.232 //

children.text: rogāḥ sarve vilīyante kuṣṭhāni sakalāni ca /
children.translated_text: All diseases are dissolved, and all <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases) as well,
for those devoted to the worship of the sun and always engaged in devotion to the guru. // Rmañj_6.233 //
This mercury preparation, named <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>, has been revealed
by <s>Śiva</s>, the compassionate-souled, for the benefit of devotees. // Rmañj_6.234 //
<s>Sarveśvararasa</s> (The Lord-of-All Preparation)
One <s>pala</s> each of killed copper, mica, and iron, and one <s>pala</s> of cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>),

should be ground with [the juices of] <s>jambīra</s> (citron), <s>unmatta</s> (Datura), <s>bhārgī</s> (Clerodendrum), <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia), <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), and <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s> (Strychnos). // Rmañj_6.235 //

children.text: mardyaṃ hayārijair drāvaiḥ pratyekaṃ ca dinaṃ dinam /
children.translated_text: It should be ground with the juices of <s>hayāri</s> (aconite) plants, each one day after day;

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaṃ mardyaṃ tadgolaṃ vastraveṣṭitam // Rmañj_6.236 //
children.translated_text: thus it should be ground for seven days, and the bolus should be wrapped in cloth. // Rmañj_6.236 //
It should be steamed in a sand-bath apparatus (<s>vālukāyantra</s>) for three days with gentle fire;

children.text: ādāya cūrṇayet sarvaṃ palaikaṃ yojayedviṣam // Rmañj_6.237 //
children.translated_text: then taking it out, one should powder everything and add one <s>pala</s> of <s>viṣa</s> (aconite). // Rmañj_6.237 //
