sudden [abnormal] arising of the senses — these are the signs of <s>sannipāta</s> (combined derangement of the three humors). // Rmañj_10.5 //

children.text: śarīraṃ śītalaṃ yasya prakṛter vikṛtir bhavet /
children.translated_text: He whose body becomes cold, whose nature undergoes alteration —

children.text: tatrāriṣṭaṃ samāsena vyāptaṃ tatra nibodha me // Rmañj_10.6 //
children.translated_text: there the fatal prognostic sign (<s>ariṣṭa</s>) is present in brief; understand this from me. // Rmañj_10.6 //
He who delights in foul speech and is angered by virtuous speech,
and he who suddenly cannot hear — one should declare him to be one whose life has departed. // Rmañj_10.7 //

children.text: yo vā gandhaṃ na gṛhṇāti dīpe śānte ca mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who does not perceive smell, and a person when the lamp is extinguished,

children.text: divājyotīṃṣi yaścāpi jvalitāni ca paśyati // Rmañj_10.8 //
children.translated_text: and he who sees luminous bodies during the day as if blazing, // Rmañj_10.8 //

children.text: candraṃ sūryaprabhaṃ paśyet sūryaṃ vā candravarcasam /
children.translated_text: he who sees the moon with the radiance of the sun, or the sun with the luster of the moon,

children.text: taḍidvātoṣitān meghān nirmale gagane carān // Rmañj_10.9 //
children.translated_text: clouds with lightning, wind, and heat moving in a clear sky, // Rmañj_10.9 //
and he who [sees] the sky crowded with aerial chariots, vehicles, and palaces,

children.text: yaśca nīlaṃ mūrtimantam antarikṣaṃ ca paśyati // Rmañj_10.10 //
children.translated_text: and he who sees the atmosphere as dark and embodied — // Rmañj_10.10 //

children.text: yastūṣṇam iva gṛhṇāti śītamuṣṇaṃ ca śītavat /
children.translated_text: he who perceives what is hot as cold, and cold as hot —

children.text: saṃjātaḥ saṃśayo yasya taṃ vadanti gatāyuṣam // Rmañj_10.11 //
children.translated_text: for whom such confusion has arisen, they declare him to be one whose life has departed. // Rmañj_10.11 //
A man who perceives things in a reversed manner, and other [abnormalities],
[who sees] the earth as if enveloped by smoke, mist, and garments — // Rmañj_10.12 //
He who sees the world as if burning, or the earth as if flooded by water,
or the ground with eighteen kinds of lines —

children.text: jyotsnādarśe hi toyeṣu chāyāṃ yaśca na paśyati /
children.translated_text: he who does not see his reflection in moonlight, mirrors, or water,

children.text: paśyatyekāṅgahīnāṃ ca vaikṛtaṃ cāpi paśyati // Rmañj_10.14 //
children.translated_text: and sees [himself] missing a limb, or sees a distortion —
a man who [sees] the approach of dogs, crows, herons, vultures, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>,
<s>piśācas</s> (demons), serpents, and <s>nāgas</s>, even in distorted [form] —

children.text: hrīśriyau yasya naśyetāṃ teja ojaḥ smṛtis tathā /
children.translated_text: he whose modesty, prosperity, luster, vitality, and memory are destroyed,
and he who yawns without cause — for him, death is beyond doubt.
He whose lower lip droops while the upper one stands raised,

children.text: pāśaśaṅkā bhavedyasya durlabhaṃ tasya jīvitam // Rmañj_10.17 //
children.translated_text: he who has the apprehension of a noose — for him, life is hard to attain.

children.text: kuṭilā sphuṭitā vāpi suptā yasya ca nāsikā /
children.translated_text: He whose nose is crooked, or cracked, or numb,

children.text: avasphūryati magnā vā sa parāsurasaṃśayam // Rmañj_10.18 //
children.translated_text: or twitches, or is sunken — for him, death is beyond doubt.

children.text: svarūpaṃ paranetreṣu puttikāṃ yo na paśyati /
children.translated_text: When one does not see one's own reflection or the pupil in the eyes of others,

children.text: yadā hi paṭudṛṣṭiśca tadā mṛtyur adūrataḥ // Rmañj_10.19 //
children.translated_text: when one's vision becomes sharp [unnaturally] — then death is not far.
When one somehow sees oneself as earless,

children.text: na sa jīvati loke'smin kālena kavalīkṛtaḥ // Rmañj_10.20 //
children.translated_text: that person does not live in this world — he is swallowed by time.

children.text: rātrau dāho bhavedyasya divā śītaṃ ca jāyate /
children.translated_text: He who has burning [sensation] at night and cold during the day,
with throat filled with <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) — death is certain, without doubt.
He whose feet are cold, whose navel region is cold,

children.text: śirastāpo bhavedyasya tasya mṛtyurna saṃśayaḥ // Rmañj_10.22 //
children.translated_text: and whose head has heat — for him, death is certain, without doubt.
He whose exhalation ("huṃ" sound) is cold while his blowing ("phut" sound) is fire-like,

children.text: sadā dāho bhavedyasya tasya mṛtyurna saṃśayaḥ // Rmañj_10.23 //
children.translated_text: he who always has burning sensation — for him, death is certain, without doubt.

children.text: arundhatīṃ dhruvaṃ caiva viṣṇostrīṇi padāni ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Arundhatī</s>, <s>Dhruva</s> (the pole star), and the three steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s> —

children.text: hīnāyudho na paśyanti caturthaṃ mātṛmaṇḍalam // Rmañj_10.24 //
children.translated_text: one with diminished weapons [senses] does not see [these]; the fourth is the circle of the mothers (<s>mātṛmaṇḍala</s>).
He who sees the disc of the sun without rays, and fire without radiance —
that person does not live beyond eleven months.

children.text: vātaṃ mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ yaḥ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: He who [perceives] flatulence, urine, and feces [as if they were] gold and silver,

children.text: pratyakṣamathavā svapne daśamāsaṃ na jīvati // Rmañj_10.26 //
children.translated_text: either in waking or in dream — does not live for ten months.

children.text: kvacit paśyati yo dīptaṃ svarṇavat kānanaṃ naraḥ /
children.translated_text: A man who somewhere sees a forest blazing like gold,

children.text: virūpāṇi ca bhūtāni navamāsaṃ na jīvati // Rmañj_10.27 //
children.translated_text: and misshapen beings — does not live for nine months.

children.text: sthūlāṅgo'pi kṛśaḥ kṛśo'pi sahasā sthūlatvamālambate śyāmo vā kanakaprabho yadi bhavedgauro'pi kṛṣṇacchaviḥ /
children.translated_text: A stout-bodied person becomes thin; a thin person suddenly becomes stout; a dark person becomes golden-hued; a fair person becomes dark-skinned;

children.text: dhīro dhīratayārthadharmanipuṇaḥ śāntopakārī pumān ityevaṃ prakṛte tu śāntacalanaṃ māsyaṣṭame mṛtyudam // Rmañj_10.28 //
children.translated_text: a courageous man skilled in wealth and <s>dharma</s>, steady, peaceful, and helpful — when such a change occurs in one's natural constitution, it causes death in the eighth month.

children.text: pīḍā bhavetpāṇitale ca jihvāmūlaṃ samūlaṃ rudhiraṃ ca kṛṣṇam /
children.translated_text: When there is pain in the palm, and the root of the tongue together with [its] base and the blood become black,

children.text: vṛddhiṃ naraḥ kāmapi yanna dṛṣṭvā jīvenmanuṣyaḥ sa hi saptamāsān // Rmañj_10.29 //
children.translated_text: and a man does not see any growth — that person lives for seven months.

children.text: madhyāṅgulīnāṃ tritayaṃ viraktaṃ rogaṃ vinā śuṣyati yasya kaṇṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The three middle fingers become discolored; the throat dries up without disease;

children.text: muhurmuhuḥ prasravaṇaṃ ca jāḍyaṃ ṣaṣṭhe ca māse pralayaṃ prayāti // Rmañj_10.30 //
children.translated_text: frequent urination and stupor [appear] — in the sixth month, he goes to dissolution.

children.text: yasya na sphuraṇaṃ kiṃcid vidyate yasya karmaṇi /
children.translated_text: He in whom there is no pulsation whatsoever in his activities —

children.text: so'vaśyaṃ pañcame māsi skandhārūḍho gamiṣyati // Rmañj_10.31 //
children.translated_text: he will certainly depart, mounted on a shoulder-bier, in the fifth month.

children.text: yasya na sphurate jyotiḥ pīḍite nayanadvaye /
children.translated_text: He in whose two eyes no light flashes when they are pressed —

children.text: maraṇaṃ tasya nirdiṣṭaṃ caturthe māsi niścitam // Rmañj_10.32 //
children.translated_text: his death is declared certain in the fourth month.

children.text: spandate vṛṣaṇo yasya na kiṃcidapi pīḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He whose testicle pulsates without any pressure at all —

children.text: tṛtīye māsi so'vaśyaṃ yamaloke gamiṣyati // Rmañj_10.33 //
children.translated_text: in the third month, he will certainly go to the world of <s>Yama</s> (the god of death).

children.text: tārā divā candraprabhaṃ niśānte yo vidyutaṃ paśyati caiva śvabhre /
children.translated_text: He who sees stars during the day, moonlight at dawn, lightning in a pit,

children.text: indrāyudhaṃ vā svayameva rātrau māsadvaye tasya vadanti nāśam // Rmañj_10.34 //
children.translated_text: or a rainbow by itself at night — they say his destruction [comes] in two months.

children.text: yasya jānugataṃ marma na kiṃcidapi ceṣṭitam /
children.translated_text: He whose vital point at the knee shows no movement whatsoever —

children.text: māsānte maraṇaṃ tasya na kenāpi vilambyate // Rmañj_10.35 //
children.translated_text: at the end of one month, death comes to him, delayed by no one.

children.text: kaniṣṭhāṅguliparva syāt kṛṣṇaṃ ca madhyamaṃ yadā /
children.translated_text: When the joint of the little finger becomes black, and the middle [joint] as well,
a man is said to have exhausted his lifespan — within eighteen days.

children.text: ghṛte taile jale vāpi darpaṇe yasya dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: He who sees himself without a head in ghee, oil, water, or a mirror —
he lives for one fortnight.
He for whom coldness, yogurt, food, and drinks become heat-producing,
and the cool-rayed [moon] becomes beautiful and laughing, and extremely pure —

children.text: na vetti vai cāruhitaṃ na coṣṇaṃ vetti yo naraḥ /
children.translated_text: a man who does not perceive what is pleasant or what is hot —

children.text: kālajñānena samproktaṃ pakṣamekaṃ sa jīvati // Rmañj_10.39 //
children.translated_text: by the science of time-knowledge, it is declared he lives for one fortnight.
He whose three [parts] — the heart, hands, and feet — dry up instantly

children.text: hṛdayaṃ hastapādau ca daśarātraṃ sa jīvati // Rmañj_10.40 //
children.translated_text: immediately after bathing — he lives for ten nights.
The tip of the nose, the tip of the tongue, and the eyes together with the seal of the lips —

children.text: yo na paśyetpurādṛṣṭaṃ saptarātraṃ sa jīvati // Rmañj_10.41 //
children.translated_text: he who cannot see [these] that were previously visible — he lives for seven nights.

children.text: dhārā bindusamā yasya patate ca mahītale /
children.translated_text: He whose stream [of urine] falls to the ground in separate drops —
death arises after seven days — thus it is declared by the science of time-knowledge.
Now I shall describe the characteristics of the shadow-person (<s>chāyāpuruṣa</s>),
by the mere knowledge of which a person becomes a knower of the three times.
Even when death is far away, by what method it is perceived —

children.text: taṃ vadanti samāsena yathoddiṣṭaṃ śivāgame // Rmañj_10.44 //
children.translated_text: that they describe in brief, as taught in the <s>Śivāgama</s>.
Going to a solitary, uninhabited place, with the sun at one's back,
gazing steadily at one's own shadow, concentrated on the neck region,
then one should look at the sky — then one sees <s>Śaṃkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>);

children.text: aṣṭottaraśataṃ japtvā tato vai dṛśyate śubham // Rmañj_10.46 //
children.translated_text: having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, then indeed the auspicious [form] is seen.
Resembling pure crystal, bearing various forms — <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>);
by the practice of this yoga for six months, one becomes the lord of earth-dwelling beings.

children.text: varṣadvayena he nātha kartā hartā svayaṃ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Within two years, O Lord, one becomes the creator, the remover, the master himself;

children.text: trikālajñatvam āpnoti sa yogī nātra saṃśayaḥ // Rmañj_10.48 //
children.translated_text: one attains knowledge of the three times — that <s>yogī</s>, without doubt.
By the practice thus performed, nothing remains unattainable;

children.text: tadrūpaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ ca paśyati vyomni nirmale // Rmañj_10.49 //
children.translated_text: but if one sees that form in black color in the clear sky —

children.text: ṣaṇmāsān mṛtyumāpnoti sa yogī nātra saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: that <s>yogī</s> will meet death within six months, without doubt.

children.text: pīto vyādhibhayaṃ rakto nīlo hatyāṃ vinirdiśet // Rmañj_10.50 //
children.translated_text: Yellow [indicates] danger from disease; red [indicates] danger from violent death; blue designates murder.
When this own form appears in various colors, great agitation arises.

children.text: pādau gulphaṃ ca jaṭharaṃ vināśakṛśatā bhavet // Rmañj_10.51 //
children.translated_text: Disappearance of the feet, ankles, or abdomen indicates emaciation [leading to death];

children.text: ardhavarṣeṇa varṣe vā jīvanvarṣadvayena na vā /
children.translated_text: within half a year, a year, or certainly not [living] two years.

children.text: vināśo dakṣiṇe bāhau svabandhur mriyate dhruvam // Rmañj_10.52 //
children.translated_text: Disappearance [of the shadow] on the right arm — one's own kinsman certainly dies;

children.text: vāmabāhau tathā bhāryā vinaśyati na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: on the left arm, the wife perishes, without doubt.
Disappearance of the head and both right arms foretells death.

children.text: aśiro māsamaraṇaṃ vinā jaṅghe divā nava /
children.translated_text: Without a head — death within a month; without legs — nine days;
with eight [days] due to the loss of the shoulders; when the shadow vanishes — instantly.
By bathing at sacred fords, charity, austerity, meritorious deeds,
<s>japa</s> (recitation), and the yoga of knowledge — the binding of time [i.e., postponement of death] is achieved.
The <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) described earlier and the pill called <s>Mṛtajīvanī</s> (Reviver of the Dead) —

children.text: naraiḥ sevyā yathoktaṃ ca paraṃ kālasya bandhanam // Rmañj_10.56 //
children.translated_text: these should be consumed by people as prescribed — that is the supreme binding of time.
Therefore the body should be protected, for it is the instrument for [attaining] <s>dharma</s> and the rest;
these <s>doṣas</s> (bodily humors), residing in <s>dhātus</s> (tissues) and <s>malas</s> (waste products), destroy the body.
By the intelligent <s>Śālinātha</s>, the son of <s>Vaidyanātha</s>,
having examined and extracted from the <s>śāstras</s>, this <s>Rasamañjarī</s> (Bouquet of Mercury) was composed.
